blocks.body:
This is a compact learning path built from the full Colombian Minnesota cultural intelligence brief. Use the evidence as a starting hypothesis, not a script. The person or household in front of you is still the authority on their own life.

  • Open this brief when the origin is Colombia. High school and college numbers do not mean there is no language need. Ask which Spanish, and who should be in the room.
  • Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity. Practitioner-based means Tuesday: name Colombia; book qualified Spanish AND ask; two surnames; no cartel joke; no SSN theater on the first screen; no harvesting Colombian staff; do not collect status you do not need. Employee groups may fact-check. They do not veto armed-conflict memory, Afro-Colombian and indigenous streams, ICE climate, or the Mexican default because a Minimization room is uncomfortable.
  • Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 9,431; Twin Cities 70.1%; Greater Minnesota 29.9%; age 17 or younger 25.6%; 65+ 4.4%; foreign-born 41.5%; language other than English (5+) 40.0%; English less than very well 16.3%; high school or higher 95.1%; bachelor’s or higher 52.1%; median household income about $69,000; poverty 7.1%; owner 54.6%; average household 2.19; uninsured 11.4%. Date Compass. Do not invent other rates. Do not copy Mexican or Ecuadorian numbers onto this page.
  • Nothing from the depth this program requires was kept at full depth. This copy is a living candidate: staff keep a stable doorway until you or an Equity Director in the administration promote.
blocks.heading: How to use this guide

blocks.body:
This brief is about Colombian people as a people with a country — Andean, Caribbean, Pacific, llanos, Amazon — and a Minnesota community the building will mash into Mexican if you let it. This is not Mexican. It is not Ecuadorian as a synonym. It is not one Spanish. Paisa, costeño, bogotano, vallecaucano are not an accent test you run in the lobby. Afro-Colombian and indigenous peoples exist inside the republic. Ask this household. Do not invent a Minnesota indigenous-language speaker count.

Who this is

A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Paternalism is one Latino blob, one “Spanish interpreter,” a cartel joke as icebreaker, and an English form because Compass bachelor’s attainment looks high.

Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Colombian ancestry near 9,431. About 70.1 percent Twin Cities, about 29.9 percent Greater Minnesota — not an afterthought. About 25.6 percent age 17 or younger; about 4.4 percent 65+. About 41.5 percent foreign-born. Language other than English (age 5+) 40.0 percent; English less than “very well” 16.3 percent. High school or higher 95.1 percent; bachelor’s or higher 52.1 percent. Poverty 7.1 percent. Uninsured 11.4 percent. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A Medellín professional, a Caribbean-coast household, an Afro-Colombian student, a U.S.-born nurse, a Greater Minnesota family, a person who left because of conflict and will not name it in the lobby, a second-generation kid who uses English with friends and Spanish with an elder — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

blocks.body:
Colombia is not one people inside one flag. Andean interior, Caribbean coast, Pacific, llanos, Amazon. Afro-Colombian nations and communities. Indigenous nations — Wayuu, Nasa, Embera, and others — inside the republic. Mestizo majority narratives do not erase those histories. Shared Spanish is not shared culture.

History for the meeting

Spanish colonial rule, Catholic mission, African enslavement, indigenous survival, a republic, and a half-century of armed conflict produced the streams you will meet. “Hispanic” on a U.S. form is an ethnicity checkbox. People in this page check white, Black, American Indian, other, two or more.

What people brought

What people brought: regional Spanish, kinship, parish and later evangelical church, professional and trade skill, and a living memory of a state and of a war that is not one war. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one Latino module, often one interpreter labeled Spanish, a Mexican default, and a drug-war headline someone thought was icebreaker.

History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with coffee, a telenovela, or a cartel sentence.

Homeland is not one city. Bogotá is not Medellín. Cali is not Barranquilla. The Pacific is not the Caribbean. Regional Spanish, food, and some kinship patterns shift. Confirm the place if they name it. Do not referee paisa versus costeño in a waiver meeting. Listen.

Homeland

In the United States, Florida, New York, and New Jersey hold large Colombian communities. Minnesota is not Miami. Do not import a Doral picture onto a Ramsey County lobby.

Minnesota

In Minnesota: Twin Cities 70.1 percent; Greater Minnesota 29.9 percent — not an afterthought. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Colombia.

blocks.body:
Colombian Minnesota is not an IRCA file and not a 1975 poster. Professional and family streams; internal displacement as a named Colombian fact (desplazados); later asylum and, for some, Temporary Protected Status as a possible U.S. path — pattern now, not a Minnesota count. Do not invent a TPS number. Do not collect status you do not need.

Foundational events

Armed conflict — guerrilla, paramilitary, state, 2016 peace, later violence in some regions — is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. It is not every household. The U.S. drug war sat on top of that stack and still sits in a lobby joke. You do not make the joke.

Who you meet

The desk in 2026 meets U.S.-born children, mixed-status households, a professional who does not need an interpreter and whose elder does, and a person who will not put a relative’s name on a form. Compass foreign-born 41.5 percent (ACS 2019–2023) — dated, not a personality.

If you only know “immigrant” or only know “cartel,” you will miss them.

Family is not one size. Some households look nuclear on an English form and still carry obligation to a parent who does not read the form. Some are extended. Compass: average household size about 2.19; about 34.9 percent live alone. That is an average, not a personality and not “they don’t do family.” Ask who should be in the room.

Who is in the household

Mixed-status is structure for some. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat unmatched last names or a missing SSN as fraud until you have a reason.

Who speaks

Familismo is a hypothesis, not a rule. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

Minnesota law still stands. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. You still see a family. Do not skip the report and call it respeto. Do not use a child as interpreter.

Catholic majority in many streams — not all. The parish may be the trusted channel. Evangelical and Pentecostal churches are large in some rooms. Afro-diasporic practice exists in some coastal families; do not exoticize, and do not assume.

Streams

Do not make a priest or a pastor the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one parish and call it consultation.

Practice

Holy Week, fiestas families name, and funeral obligation can collide with your calendar. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict.

Help that looks like a report is not help. Religious framing of disability, mental health, or gender can sit next to a fierce wish for services. You can hold both.

Handshake is common in many rooms. Follow this room. A slight nod with an elder is safer than a hard first-name hello you assume is warmth. Some streams greet familiars with a cheek kiss — do not initiate because a training slide said Latinos are tactile.

Titles

Titles until invited: Señor, Señora, Don, Doña. Use the last name you were given — and remember there may be two. Usted versus tú varies by region; a qualified interpreter matches register. You do not correct it.

This room

Elders first. Greet the people in the room, not only the English speaker.

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. Cross-gender touch: follow this room.

blocks.body:
Two surnames is the default in much of Spanish-language naming: apellido paterno then apellido materno. A U.S. database that keeps one surname invents a person. That invented name then follows them through MHCP, child welfare, and school. It is a gate.

How to file

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Do not drop accents as a joke. Given names may be Spanish, indigenous, English, or both. Ask.

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default.

blocks.body:
Minnesota holds a Colombian community large enough for a Compass profile — about 9,431 (ACS 2019–2023) — and large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment. Greater Minnesota is 29.9 percent. Do not write this people as a Minneapolis anecdote.

Places

Places, not a blob: Twin Cities; inner-ring suburbs; Greater Minnesota towns. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume the person in front of you has been downtown.

Partners

Partners: parishes families name; civic groups this family names; CLUES is a Latino door, not a Colombian community. CECLC is a department door, not the whole. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Colombian staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. Hispanic Heritage Month is not consultation. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

blocks.body:
To be Colombian in Minnesota is to be placed in a U.S. checkbox that holds Mexican as the default and a news cycle that holds a cartel as the icebreaker. There is a peoplehood here the mash deletes: regional Spanish, Afro-Colombian and indigenous histories, professional and working-class lives, conflict memory for some and a history class for others.

In this state

Mexican Minnesota is the largest Latino origin in this state. That fact becomes a harm when the building treats Mexican Spanish as the Latino default. A costeño household, a paisa household, and an Afro-Colombian household are not variants of Mexico.

In the U.S. racial order, Hispanic is ethnicity, not race. Colorism inside this page is real. Afro-Colombian people exist — ask, do not mash them into historic African American, and do not bleach them into a mestizo story. Drug-war stigma is a named harm. You do not write it as ethnicity.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to this family.

blocks.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts. ERGs may fact-check this page. They do not get a veto because a fact is hard to say.

Named harms

Drug-war stigma is a named harm. A cartel joke, a sniffing mime, a “where the cocaine is from” icebreaker — those are closed doors. You do not write cartel as ethnicity. You do not put it on a last name as a risk score.

ICE and enforcement climate is structure for some. Mixed-status households skip clinic when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

Conflict trauma sits in some rooms. It is not a personality and not every household. The Mexican default will talk over this page if you let it. Colorism is real. Machismo is a named harm, not “that’s culture.” Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting.

Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Colombian cultural community: about 9,431; Twin Cities 70.1%; Greater Minnesota 29.9%; age 17 or younger 25.6%; 65+ 4.4%; foreign-born 41.5%; language other than English (age 5+) 40.0%; English less than “very well” 16.3%; English only 60.0%; high school or higher (25+) 95.1%; bachelor’s or higher 52.1%; median household income about $69,000 (2022 dollars, averaged); poverty 7.1%; owner-occupied 54.6%; average household size 2.19; uninsured 11.4%.

Counts

Date Compass. Do not invent a TPS count or an indigenous-language speaker count. Do not copy Mexican, Ecuadorian, or Cuban numbers onto this page. Counts disagree across ACS vintages and definitions. Date the number you cite.

What the count is not

blocks.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: CLAS Spanish is not one Spanish. Colombian regional Spanish is not a Mexican interpreter accent test. A child as interpreter is a closed door and a harm. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. High bachelor’s attainment is not “no interpreter.”

Names: two surnames. The database that keeps one invents a person. Unmatched last names are not fraud by default.

SSN on the first screen, hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral. Mixed-status households will bounce if the first field feels like enforcement. Do not collect status you do not need.

Child welfare and disability: help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow law.

Enforcement climate: people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance.

Drug-war stigma in the lobby is a gate. You do not write cartel as ethnicity.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Greater Minnesota is 29.9 percent — a Minneapolis default is a gate.

Workforce: Colombian staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat them.

Mexican default is a gate. Disaggregate or you invented a people.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that never learned that Spanish is not the people.

This is a compact learning path built from the full Cuban Minnesota cultural intelligence brief. Use the evidence as a starting hypothesis, not a script. The person or household in front of you is still the authority on their own life.

  • Open this brief when the origin is Cuban. Do not run a Puerto Rican citizenship script, and do not collect status you do not need.
  • Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity. Practitioner-based means Tuesday: name Cuba; book qualified Spanish AND ask; two surnames; do not mash with Mexican or Puerto Rican; no one-exile speech; no SSN theater you do not need; no harvesting Cuban staff; do not collect status you do not need. Employee groups may fact-check. They do not veto 1959 politics, Mariel, colorism, or later-stream difference because a Minimization room is uncomfortable.
  • Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 9,406; Twin Cities 67.3%; Greater Minnesota 32.7%; age 17 or younger 34.1%; 65+ 8.9%; foreign-born 21.9%; language other than English (5+) 39.3%; English less than very well 11.4%; high school or higher 82.2%; bachelor’s or higher 33.3%; median household income about $90,000; poverty 10.5%; owner 45.0%; average household 2.84; uninsured 4.3%; disability 21.5%. Date Compass. Do not invent other rates. Do not copy Mexican or Puerto Rican numbers onto this page.
  • Nothing from the depth this program requires was kept at full depth. This copy is a living candidate: staff keep a stable doorway until you or an Equity Director in the administration promote.

blocks.body:
This brief is about Cuban people as a people with a country and a Minnesota community the building will mash into Mexican — or into Puerto Rican — if you let it. This is not Mexican. It is not interchangeable with Puerto Rican. Puerto Rican is U.S. citizenship under the Jones Act (1917). Cuban is not that file. 1959, Mariel (1980), 1994 balseros, and later streams are not one exile story. Spanish is Caribbean Spanish, not Mexican.

Who this is

A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Paternalism is one Latino blob, one “Spanish interpreter,” a 1959 speech you give a U.S.-born twenty-year-old, and collecting status because you learned the word Mariel.

Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Cuban ancestry near 9,406. About 67.3 percent Twin Cities, about 32.7 percent Greater Minnesota — not an afterthought. About 34.1 percent age 17 or younger; about 8.9 percent 65+. About 21.9 percent foreign-born — which means a large share was born here. Language other than English (age 5+) 39.3 percent; English less than “very well” 11.4 percent. Poverty 10.5 percent. Owner 45.0 percent. Disability 21.5 percent. Date the number you use. Do not invent a cause. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A 1960s exile elder, a Mariel arrival, a 1994 balsero, a later-stream parent, a U.S.-born nurse, an Afro-Cuban student, a Greater Minnesota household, a person who left 1959 politics and still shows up at a parish — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

blocks.body:
Cuban peoplehood is older than 1959 and older than Miami. An island in the Caribbean; Spanish colonial rule; African enslavement; Chinese contract labor; a republic; a revolution. White Cuban, Afro-Cuban, mixed. Mestizaje narratives do not erase Black Cuba. Shared Spanish is not shared culture with Mexico. Shared Caribbean is not shared culture with Puerto Rico.

History for the meeting

What people brought: Caribbean Spanish, kinship, Catholic and Afro-Cuban religious practice, professional and trade skill, and a living memory of a state that some fled and some still argue. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one Latino module, often one interpreter labeled Spanish, a Mexican default, and a Miami picture that is not this map.

What people brought

History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a cigar, a classic car, or a 1959 tourism sentence.

blocks.body:
If 1975 is the foundational event of Vietnamese Minnesota, Cuban Minnesota does not get one year that covers the lobby. It gets a stack, and you will misread the room if you pick the wrong one.

Foundational events

1959–early 1960s: revolution, first-wave exile — often more connected, more already professional. That is a stream, not a virtue ranking. Freedom Flights. Mariel 1980 — a different class mix, a stigma that still sits in some rooms. 1994 balseros. Wet foot/dry foot ended January 2017. Later irregular arrivals via other countries. U.S.-born children in every stream.

Who you meet

Cuban Adjustment Act (1966) is literacy for the desk: a path some people can use after a year of presence. It is not a speech. It is not permission to collect status you do not need. It is not Puerto Rican citizenship.

The desk in 2026 meets a third-generation English-dominant adult, an elder who needs Caribbean Spanish, and last year’s arrival. Compass foreign-born 21.9 percent (ACS 2019–2023) is the dated share — not “everyone is an exile.” 1959 is literacy. It is not a speech you give the family.

Elders first. Greet the people in the room, not only the English speaker.

blocks.body:
Two surnames is the default in much of Spanish-language naming: apellido paterno then apellido materno. A U.S. database that keeps one surname invents a person. That invented name then follows them through MHCP, child welfare, and school. It is a gate.

How to file

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Do not drop accents as a joke. Given names may be Spanish, English, or both. Ask.

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default.

blocks.body:
1 January 1959 — the revolution / the exile, depending on the room. In many Cuban American rooms this is grief and politics. It is not a party. Do not put a slogan on a case note. Do not celebrate or condemn in the file. Listen if they name it.

Calendar

Independence 20 May appears in some exile calendars. 10 October. Ask. Hispanic Heritage Month is a U.S. poster, not this people.

Calendar clicks are literacy for scheduling. They are not community engagement and not a day off the work. Do not put “Latino holiday” on a case note.

blocks.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Cuban Minnesotans 25 and older, about 82.2 percent high school or higher; about 33.3 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. Streams differ: first-wave professional memory is not Mariel and is not last year’s arrival. About 21.9 percent of the community is foreign-born. A large share of children are U.S.-born. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Spanish and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only form is the gate. Do not skip the interpreter because a 1959 story said professional, and do not assume illiteracy because the stream is later.

Do not use a child as interpreter. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter.

blocks.body:
Hospitality: food, drink, time. Accepting a little is courtesy. You still keep medical and legal clocks.

In the home

Titles and elders. Shoes: follow the household. Do not photograph an altar — Catholic or Afro-Cuban. Do not ask an elder to explain the revolution as entertainment.

Time

Punctuality: social time can run long. Work, clinic, and court time should be treated as on time. Do not write a “Latino time” joke in a case note.

Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice. Ask whether they agree with the plan. Do not take a smile as consent.

This is the CLAS Spanish line — and Spanish is not the people. Caribbean Spanish is not Mexican Spanish and not Andean Spanish. Book a qualified Spanish interpreter AND ask this household. Register matters.

Language

Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among those 5 and older, 39.3 percent speak a language other than English; 11.4 percent speak English less than “very well”; English only 60.7 percent. Date the number. A large U.S.-born share is English-dominant. The elder may not be. Do not skip the interpreter because Compass LEP looks modest.

Do not use a child as interpreter. Do not make a a Cuban coworker the interpreter. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

Not one playlist. Son, salsa, rumba, timba, trova — origin names the sound. A Mexican default playlist in a Cuban waiting room is the mash in speakers.

Variation

A festival stage is not engagement. A playlist is not language access. A rumba or a liturgy is not staff entertainment.

Knowing that music is public life will not write the waiver. It will stop you from treating one Heritage Month speaker as the community.

A baseball sticker is not proof the elder reads English.

blocks.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts. ERGs may fact-check this page. They do not get a veto because a fact is hard to say.

Named harms

1959 intra-community politics still split some rooms — flag, exile, later arrivals who did not come as anti-communist heroes. You do not referee. You do not put it on a case note as color. Mariel stigma is a named harm. It is not a risk score.

Colorism is real. White Cuban default will talk over Afro-Cuban if you let it. ICE and enforcement climate is structure for some later streams. Do not collect status you do not need. Cuban Adjustment Act is literacy, not a reason to collect status.

Compass disability 21.5 percent (ACS 2019–2023). Date it. Do not invent a cause. Do not skip screening.

LGBTQ Cubans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting.

Access

Believe reported pain. Do not skip screening. Do not fold this history into Tuskegee or into a generic “immigrant mistrust” slide. Streams differ: an elder of 1961 and a 2022 arrival do not share a clinic story.

Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Do not use a child as interpreter in a health encounter. Colorism in the clinic is a named harm if staff treat Afro-Cuban as a different file.

blocks.body:
There is no Cuban uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Guayabera and white at some public events are not a daily costume, and not yours to request for a Heritage Month photo.

Dress

Colorism and hair texture are real. White Cuban, Afro-Cuban, mixed. Afro-Cuban hair is not the CROWN Act chapter copied over — and you still do not touch, still do not police. Do not rank race off skin or hair in a case note.

Do not ask if they “still wear the costume.” Ask the person, with gender match if they want it.

This is a compact learning path built from the full Ecuadorian Minnesota cultural intelligence brief. Use the evidence as a starting hypothesis, not a script. The person or household in front of you is still the authority on their own life.

  • Open this brief when the origin is Ecuador. Ask which language is spoken at home. This is not Colombian as a synonym.
  • Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity. Practitioner-based means Tuesday: name Ecuador; book qualified Spanish AND ask; Kichwa, Shuar, or another indigenous language on the line when that is the home language; two surnames; no SSN theater on the first screen; no harvesting Ecuadorian staff; do not collect status you do not need. Employee groups may fact-check. They do not veto indigenous languages, mixed-status households, ICE climate, or the Mexican default because a Minimization room is uncomfortable.
  • Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 18,271; Twin Cities 94.0%; Greater Minnesota 6.0%; age 17 or younger 42.7%; 65+ 2.1%; foreign-born 49.8%; language other than English (5+) 76.4%; English less than very well 44.6%; high school or higher 57.6%; bachelor’s or higher 21.3%; median household income about $57,000; poverty 20.2%; owner 65.8%; average household 3.82; uninsured 21.6%. Date Compass. Do not invent other rates. Do not copy Mexican or Colombian numbers onto this page.
  • Nothing from the depth this program requires was kept at full depth. This copy is a living candidate: staff keep a stable doorway until you or an Equity Director in the administration promote.
blocks.heading: How to use this guide

blocks.body:
This brief is about Ecuadorian people as a people with a country — Costa, Sierra, Amazon/Oriente, Galápagos — and a Minnesota community the building will mash into Mexican if you let it. This is not Mexican. It is not Colombian as a synonym. It is not one Spanish. Indigenous languages may be in the home: Kichwa, Shuar, others. Compass notes the possibility; it is not a count of speakers. Do not invent that count. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door.

Who this is

A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Paternalism is one Latino blob, one “Spanish interpreter,” an SSN field on the first screen, and an English IEP written for a household the building never studied.

Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Ecuadorian ancestry near 18,271. About 94.0 percent Twin Cities, about 6.0 percent Greater Minnesota. About 42.7 percent age 17 or younger; about 2.1 percent 65+. About 49.8 percent foreign-born. Language other than English (age 5+) 76.4 percent; English less than “very well” 44.6 percent. Poverty 20.2 percent. Uninsured 21.6 percent. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A Kichwa-speaking mother who does not use Spanish as a home language, an Afro-Ecuadorian student, a coastal Spanish speaker, a Sierra household that uses usted, a U.S.-born child in an English-dominant school, a professional second generation, a mixed-status kitchen table — share a Census checkbox and do not share a Tuesday.

How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

blocks.body:
Ecuador is not one people inside one flag. Costa, Sierra, Amazon/Oriente, Galápagos. Kichwa (Runa Shimi) and other indigenous nations live inside the republic. Shuar and other Amazonian peoples. Afro-Ecuadorian streams in Esmeraldas and the Valle del Chota. Mestizo majority narratives do not erase those histories. Shared Spanish is not shared culture.

History for the meeting

Spanish colonial rule, Catholic mission, indigenous survival, African enslavement on the coast, a republic, and later dollarization and emigration produced the streams you will meet. “Hispanic” on a U.S. form is an ethnicity checkbox. People in this page check white, Black, American Indian, other, two or more. The form that treats Hispanic as a race has already mashed.

What people brought

What people brought: Spanish varieties and indigenous languages, kinship, parish and later evangelical church, work knowledge, and a living memory of a state and of a crisis that moved people. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one Latino module, often one interpreter labeled Spanish, and a Mexican default.

History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with food, a hat, or a Heritage Month sentence.

Regional Spanish and indigenous languages do not travel as a blob. Do not referee Quito versus Guayaquil in a waiver meeting. Listen if they name a place.

Homeland

In the United States, New York and New Jersey hold large Ecuadorian communities. Minnesota is not Queens. Do not import a Roosevelt Avenue picture onto a Hennepin County lobby.

Minnesota

In Minnesota: Twin Cities is the Compass split — 94.0 percent. Greater Minnesota is 6.0 percent, not zero. Do not copy a Worthington plant-town default from Mexican Minnesota onto this page, and do not assume Minneapolis is every household. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Ecuador.

blocks.body:
If IRCA is a foundational settlement fact of Mexican Minnesota, Ecuadorian Minnesota is not that file. Labor and family streams; the 1999–2000 banking crisis (feriado bancario) as a named emigration wave toward Spain and the United States; later family reunification and work; secondary migration from other states.

Foundational events

The desk in 2026 meets U.S.-born children translating for parents, mixed-status households, a Kichwa household that has been here for years and still cannot get the language in the lobby, and a professional who does not need an interpreter and whose elder does. Who you meet

Enforcement is current structure. When raids or a visible ICE climate spike, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need. The desk that asks “are you legal?” on visit one has already chosen a who.

If you only know “immigrant” or only know “Latino,” you will miss them.

Family is often larger than a nuclear English form. Elders, in-laws, adult children, and cousins who are household in practice sit in the same week. Compass: average household size about 3.82. That is larger than some neighboring spines. It is not a rule. Ask who should be in the room.

Who is in the household

Mixed-status is structure: a U.S.-citizen child, a parent without status, a sibling with another path. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat unmatched last names, a grandmother as caregiver, or a missing SSN as fraud until you have a reason.

Who speaks

Familismo is a hypothesis, not a rule: obligation to kin can mean fierce showing-up and can mean a woman who never signs for herself. Both can be true. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

Minnesota law still stands. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. You still see a family. Do not skip the report and call it respeto. Do not use a child as interpreter.

Streams

Do not make a priest, a pastor, or a healer the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one parish and call it consultation. Do not treat evangelical growth as the evolved version of Catholic, or indigenous practice as witchcraft.

Practice

Holy Week, fiestas families name, and funeral obligation can collide with your calendar. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict.

Titles

This room

Elders first. Greet the people in the room, not only the English speaker.

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. Cross-gender touch: follow this room.

blocks.body:
Two surnames is the default in much of Spanish-language naming: apellido paterno then apellido materno. A U.S. database that keeps one surname invents a person. That invented name then follows them through MHCP, child welfare, and school. It is a gate.

How to file

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Do not drop accents as a joke. Given names may be Spanish, indigenous, English, or both. Some people use a middle given name as the call-name. Ask.

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default. Do not invent a hyphen and then punish the person when the hyphen moves.

Minnesota holds an Ecuadorian community large enough for a Compass profile — about 18,271 (ACS 2019–2023) — and large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment. Twin Cities 94.0 percent. Greater Minnesota 6.0 percent is not an afterthought and is not a plant-town mash with Mexican Minnesota.

Places

Places, not a blob: Twin Cities corridors and first-ring suburbs; scattered Greater Minnesota households. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume the person in front of you has been downtown.

Partners

Partners: parishes families name; civic groups this family names; CLUES is a Latino door, not an Ecuadorian community and not Greater Minnesota. CECLC is a department door, not the whole. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Ecuadorian staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. Hispanic Heritage Month is not consultation. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

blocks.body:
To be Ecuadorian in Minnesota is to be placed in a U.S. checkbox that holds Mexican as the default. There is a peoplehood here the mash deletes: Costa, Sierra, Oriente; Kichwa and other indigenous nations; Afro-Ecuadorian histories; U.S.-born lives. Spanish is not the people.

In this state

Mexican Minnesota is the largest Latino origin in this state. That fact becomes a harm when the building treats Mexican Spanish, Mexican parish, and Mexican food as the Latino default. An Andean household, a Kichwa household, and an Afro-Ecuadorian household are not variants of Mexico.

In the U.S. racial order, Hispanic is ethnicity, not race. Colorism inside this page is real. Indigenous erasure under “they all speak Spanish” is real. Afro-Ecuadorian people exist — ask, do not mash them into historic African American, and do not bleach them into a mestizo story.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to this family.

blocks.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Ecuadorian Minnesotans 25 and older, about 57.6 percent high school or higher; about 21.3 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. Do not copy Colombian or Lebanese attainment onto this page. About 42.7 percent of the community is age 17 or younger. The IEP is a gate, not a one-hour culture clash.

School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Spanish, or fluent Kichwa, and limited English is not illiterate. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed. Oral Spanish is not print Spanish. Mixtec is a Mexican door; Kichwa is this one. A Spanish IEP is still a closed door if Spanish is not the home language.

Do not use a child as interpreter. That is a closed door and a harm: it reverses respeto, it leaks adult business, and it is not CLAS. Do not invent a dropout rate on this page.

blocks.body:
Hospitality: food, drink, time. Accepting a little is courtesy. Refusing everything can read as cold. You still keep medical and legal clocks.

In the home

Titles and elders. Shoes: follow the household. Do not walk into a living room and photograph an altar. Do not touch ritual objects. Do not ask an elder to explain “your culture” as entertainment.

Time

Punctuality: social time can run long. Work, clinic, and court time should be treated as on time. Do not write a “Latino time” joke in a case note.

Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice. Confirm in the language they use. Ask whether they agree with the plan. Do not take a smile as consent.

blocks.body:
This is the CLAS Spanish line — and Spanish is not the people. Andean Spanish, coastal Spanish, and Mexican Spanish are not one interpreter accent test. Book a qualified Spanish interpreter AND ask this household. Register matters: usted, not a buddy tú, until the room says otherwise.

Language

Indigenous languages may be in the home. Kichwa. Shuar. Others. Compass notes the possibility; it is not a count of speakers. Do not invent that count. A Spanish interpreter for those households is still a closed door. Name the language on the request. A scarce interpreter is a gate, not an excuse to proceed in English only without recording the failure.

Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among those 5 and older, 76.4 percent speak a language other than English; 44.6 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number. Do not use a child as interpreter. Do not make an Ecuadorian coworker the interpreter.

A short English yes may be exhaustion, hierarchy, or the interpreter. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent. Do not write “noncompliant” when you mean “did not understand the English exception form.”

Spanish-language literature is world literature. Indigenous oral literature — Kichwa and others — is older than the Spanish file and is not “no letters.” That fact does not mean the person in the lobby can read your form — in English or in Spanish. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed.

Literacy in the lobby

You do not need to quote a novel in the lobby. You do need to know this is not a people without letters, and not a people who can all read the exception process.

Print Spanish from Spain, Mexico, or a machine translation is not automatically this household’s Spanish. CLAS is qualified language, not Google and not a child.

blocks.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts. ERGs may fact-check this page. They do not get a veto because a fact is hard to say.

Named harms

ICE and enforcement climate is structure. Mixed-status households skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need. SSN on the first screen is a gate.

Indigenous erasure under “they all speak Spanish” is a named harm. Kichwa, Shuar. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Colorism is real. The Mexican default in this state will talk over an Andean household if you let it.

Machismo is a named harm, not a joke and not “that’s culture.” Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. You still see a family.

LGBTQ Ecuadorians exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it familismo. Hispanic Heritage Month is not consultation.

blocks.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 21.6 percent without health insurance among those for whom status is determined; poverty 20.2 percent. Date them. Do not invent a diabetes or “Andean” rate. Pattern now: people delay, people use the emergency room as the door, people skip follow-up when the lobby feels like enforcement.

Access

Fear of the lobby is a health access fact. A badge, a form that asks for SSN, a child called to interpret a diagnosis, an interpreter who does not speak this Spanish or this indigenous language — these are clinical events. When enforcement spikes, people skip clinic. That is not noncompliance.

Believe reported pain. Do not skip screening. Do not fold this history into Tuskegee or into a generic “immigrant mistrust” slide. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Do not use a child as interpreter in a health encounter.

This person

Colorism and hair texture are real. Afro-Ecuadorian hair is not the CROWN Act chapter copied over — and you still do not touch, still do not police, still do not treat tightness or looseness as a professionalism problem.

Do not rank piety or indigeneity off clothing. Ask the person, with gender match if they want it.

blocks.body:
There is no single Civil Rights Movement to copy onto this page. The political literacy here is stacked: labor and family migration; the 1999–2000 banking crisis as a named wave; later work streams; and U.S. enforcement that reorganizes Tuesday. Indigenous erasure under Spanish is a named harm.

The badge

When enforcement spikes, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. A DHS badge is not automatically help. That is not paranoia. It is pattern. Do not use a crisis or a raid as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate crossing for your professional development.

Do not collect status you do not need. SSN on the first screen is a gate. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole people as a deportation score.

Service, construction, restaurants, cleaning, childcare, professional second generation, public employment. Compass median household income about $57,000; poverty 20.2 percent — averages, not this kitchen table. A small-business owner and a waiver recipient may be the same household.

Work

Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: CLAS Spanish is not one Spanish. Andean and coastal Spanish are not a Mexican interpreter accent test. Kichwa, Shuar, and other indigenous languages may be in the home. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed. A child as interpreter is a closed door and a harm. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: two surnames. The database that keeps one invents a person. Unmatched last names are not fraud by default.

SSN on the first screen, hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral. Mixed-status households will bounce if the first field feels like enforcement. Do not collect status you do not need.

Child welfare and disability: 42.7 percent age 17 or younger is a desk fact. Help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole people as a risk score. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow law.

Enforcement climate: people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater.

Workforce: Ecuadorian staff are not the interpreter pool, not the indigenous-language pool, and not the community. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat them.

Mexican default is a gate. Disaggregate or you invented a people.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that never learned that Spanish is not the people.

This is a compact learning path built from the full Ethiopian Minnesota cultural intelligence brief. Use the evidence as a starting hypothesis, not a script. The person or household in front of you is still the authority on their own life.

  • Open this brief when the household names Ethiopia and you do not yet know which people. Then move to the Oromo, Amharic, or Tigrayan door that matches.
  • Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity. Practitioner-based means Tuesday: which people and which language — Afaan Oromoo, Amharic, Tigrinya, or the language this household names — not “Ethiopian,” not Somali; no harvesting Ethiopian staff; do not referee intra-Ethiopian politics; do not fold this household into historic African American CI because both are Black. Employee groups may fact-check. They do not veto the Tigray war as current structure, a three-name form, or the fact that this Compass row is an umbrella because a Minimization room is uncomfortable.
  • Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 40,324; Twin Cities 89.4%; Greater Minnesota 10.6%; age 17 or younger 43.5%; 65+ 3.6%; foreign-born 61.7%; language other than English (5+) 74.9%; English less than very well 30.4%; high school or higher 81.5%; bachelor’s or higher 24.6%; median household income about $57,106; poverty 13.0%; owner 34.7%; renter 65.3%; average household 3.09. Date Compass. Census recodes some Oromo responses as Ethiopian. Do not invent other rates.
  • Nothing from the depth this program requires was kept at full depth. This copy is a living candidate: staff keep a stable doorway until you or an Equity Director in the administration promote.
blocks.heading: How to use this guide

blocks.body:
This brief is about Ethiopian Minnesota as Compass treats it: an umbrella count, not one people. Oromo, Amhara, Tigrayan, Gurage, Sidama, and others are not one file. If the household is Oromo, open Oromo Minnesota and book Afaan Oromoo. If Amharic is the home language, open Amharic-speaking Minnesota. If Tigrayan, book Tigrinya — Tigrinya is not Amharic. If they name Somali ancestry, open Somali Minnesota. Compass already counts respondents born in Ethiopia who list Somali ancestry as Somali, not Ethiopian.

Who this is

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Ethiopian Minnesota near 40,324. About 89.4 percent Twin Cities, about 10.6 percent Greater Minnesota. About 43.5 percent age 17 or younger; about 3.6 percent 65+. About 61.7 percent foreign-born. Language other than English (age 5+) 74.9 percent; English less than “very well” 30.4 percent. Date the number. Census recodes some people who write Oromo into Ethiopian. That is an overcount of a state name and an undercount of a people. Use these numbers as dated umbrella context, not as a personality.

Who this is not

This is not Somali. Shared Horn is not shared culture. This is not historic African American. Shared race in the United States is not shared culture. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

How to read this

The diversity inside the umbrella is the point. An Amhara Orthodox grandmother who fasts more days than the clinic has slots, an Oromo evangelical household that does not want Amharic, a Tigrayan family living the 2020–2022 war through kin, a Muslim Ethiopian household, a U.S.-born student who uses English with friends and another language with an elder — share a Compass row and do not share a Tuesday.

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

blocks.body:
Ethiopia is a state of many nations. Oromo peoplehood — Oromummaa — is a Cushitic nation of the Horn, the largest by language, with no Oromo nation-state. Amhara highland peoplehood and Amharic as a written language are older than 1974. Tigrayan peoplehood sits on both sides of a later border with Eritrea. Gurage, Sidama, and others live in Minnesota too. Ask which people they are. Do not lecture taxonomy they did not ask for.

History for the meeting

Imperial history, Orthodox Tewahedo, Islam, and a federal working language that is not everyone’s first language organized a state that was not a European colony in the way neighboring files were. That fact is literacy. It is not a rank you give the family, and it is not a reason to skip language access.

What people brought

What people brought: many languages, Orthodox fasting and Protestant and Muslim streams and Waaqeffanna, kin obligation, injera as ordinary food in many rooms, a memory of empire and of a state that won and a state that lost. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Ethiopian” checkbox, one “East African” interpreter, and often Somali because the building already has that page.

Origins did not begin in 1974. 1974 is the foundational political event of much of the first wave you will meet. It is not a speech you give the family.

Homeland is not one ethnic map. Oromia, Amhara region, Tigray, the south, Addis Ababa, and a Somali region Compass already carved out of this count. Do not draw one Ethiopia on a case note. Do not assume Addis as identity. Many Oromo people name Oromia, a region, a village, a lineage — not the capital of the state that ruled them.

Homeland

The diaspora is global: Washington D.C. as a large U.S. hub, Los Angeles, Dallas, Toronto, the Gulf, Italy. Minnesota is a real community, not the U.S. capital of it. Secondary migration and church and mosque networks pulled people here.

Minnesota

In Minnesota: Compass is 89.4 percent Twin Cities. Minneapolis parishes. Inner-ring suburbs. Greater Minnesota — including Worthington, where Ethiopian Orthodox life is public — is 10.6 percent. Do not assume Cedar-Riverside. That hub is Somali unless this family lives there. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Ethiopia.

blocks.body:
If 1991 is Somali Minnesota’s foundational political event, 1974 and what followed is the foundational event of much of this Compass row’s first wave. It is not the only stream, and it is not one people’s story.

Foundational events

The revolution overthrew Haile Selassie. The Derg and the Red Terror killed and scattered people. The 1980s famine and resettlement brought some of the first African refugees Minnesota named as Ethiopian — the state’s telling has Minnesota admitting refugees from Ethiopia from 1982. Others came through Sudan, Kenya, Europe. 1991 ended the Derg and opened another politics. Family reunification and later diversity streams followed. Unrest in the 2010s–2020s sent another Oromo wave. The 2020–2022 war in Tigray is current structure for some households.

Who you meet

Do not referee. Do not pick a side as DHS. Intra-Ethiopian tension in Minnesota rooms is real. Listen if they name it. Do not file it as a risk score.

The desk in 2026 also meets U.S.-born children — English with peers, still translating, still unable to get Afaan Oromoo or Amharic or Tigrinya in a lobby that offered Somali or “Ethiopian.” If you only know “Ethiopian refugee,” you will miss this household.

blocks.body:
Family is larger than a nuclear English form. Elders often speak first. Godparent and kin ties, adult children in the same week as a waiver, and a grandmother who is the childcare. Compass average household size 3.09 — umbrella, dated, still not Mary Jones.

Who is in the household

Who cares for a disabled adult or a child may be a son, a daughter-in-law, a sibling, not the legally recognized caregiver on the checkbox. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

Who speaks

Naming is already a who: given name plus father’s name, often no surname. Oromo names are not Amharic names. Do not invent a last name because the screen requires one. Do not assume three Somali names.

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child with the best English. That child is not the qualified interpreter. CLAS still stands. Ask who should be in the room. Minnesota law still stands. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

blocks.body:
Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo is central for many Amhara and some other households. Protestant streams — including Oromo evangelical churches — are ordinary. Islam lives in Oromo, some other Ethiopian, and adjacent Horn rooms. Waaqeffanna lives in some Oromo rooms. None is also a Tuesday. Ask. Do not assume Muslim like Somali. Do not assume Orthodox like a mash of “Ethiopian.”

Streams

Ge’ez is liturgical. It is not the interview language. Arabic may be religion, not the interview. Book the language this elder actually uses for a legal notice.

Practice

Fasting calendars are operations for many Orthodox households: Wednesday, Friday, Lent, Advent, other seasons. Medication with food, labs, morning appointments. “No-show” may be the feast you scheduled against. Ask.

Do not make a priest, a debtera, a pastor, or an imam the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one parish and call it consultation. Funerals gather family. You still keep medical and legal time. Do not photograph an iconostasis.

blocks.body:
Elders first. Ato / Weizero / Weizerit in some Amharic rooms — use the honorific until invited not to. Shoulder bumps and cheek kisses in some rooms. Follow this room.

Titles

As-salāmu ʿalaykum is not default. In a Christian Oromo or Amhara room it is already a closed door. In a Muslim room it may be ordinary. English “hello” is ordinary in the second generation. Do not perform a greeting you learned from a video.

This room

A hard handshake you assume is universal is already a closed door for some women and some elders. Many second-generation people will shake hands in English-language rooms. If a hand is not offered, nod. Do not force it.

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars. Physical contact: ask the room. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default.

Often given name plus father’s name, sometimes grandfather’s. No family surname as the database wants. Same trap as Somali, different grammar, different people. Do not invent a last name because the screen requires one. That invented name becomes a gate that follows them through MHCP, school, and child welfare.

How to file

Oromo names are not Amharic names. Do not assume three Somali names. Honorifics Ato / Weizero in some Amharic rooms are not decoration.

Ask how to say it. Ask how to file it. Pronounce it. Women may or may not take a husband’s name in U.S. records. Mother and child may not match. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not joke about names. Do not collect a clan or ethnic list as an icebreaker.

blocks.body:
Minnesota holds an Ethiopian Compass community large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment — and large enough that the building has a long habit of hearing “East African” and booking Somali. Compass: about 40,324 (ACS 2019–2023). Greater Minnesota is 10.6 percent. Do not write this umbrella as a Minneapolis anecdote.

Places

Places, not a blob: Minneapolis parishes (Debre Selam Medhanealem Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church among them); inner-ring suburbs; Worthington and other Greater Minnesota towns where Orthodox liturgy is public; Little Oromia as community naming for Oromo Twin Cities life (MNHS) — open the Oromo CI for that map; not Cedar-Riverside as the default.

Partners

Partners: Orthodox parishes families name; Protestant congregations including Oromo evangelical churches; mosques families name including Tawfiq for some Oromo households; Ethiopian Community in Minnesota as historical local door; Oromo Community of Minnesota historically — pay the door this household actually uses; SOS Amharic voter tools as proof the state already knew one of the languages; CECLC as a department door — not the whole.

Ethiopian-identified staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. A Timkat or Irreecha visit is optional professional development if you are invited. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

blocks.body:
To be filed Ethiopian in Minnesota is sometimes to be Amhara, sometimes Oromo, sometimes Tigrayan, sometimes another nation the Compass row cannot see. A state name is not peoplehood. Oromummaa is not the empire. Highland Orthodox life is not the mosque. You do not pick a side.

In this state

In this building another fact sits on top: many of these households are Black in a U.S. racial order that will file them under Somali or under historic African American and get the language, the church, and the name wrong. Shared race is not shared culture. Shared Horn geography is not shared language.

Face, elder obligation, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.

Which people. Oromo, Amhara, Tigrayan, other. Ask. The Compass row is not the answer.

Which language

Afaan Oromoo, Amharic, Tigrinya, other. An “Ethiopian interpreter” is often Amharic. That is a closed door for many Oromo and Tigrayan households. A Somali interpreter is the wrong door.

Names

Given name plus father’s name. Do not invent a last name. Oromo names are not Amharic names. Not three Somali names.

Faith is plural

Orthodox Tewahedo, Protestant, Islam, Waaqeffanna, none. Follow this room. Fasting is operations, not folklore.

Do not assume Addis. Do not referee intra-Ethiopian politics in a waiver meeting. Do not pick a side as DHS.

Work and school as a family project

A restaurant, a parking shift, a second-generation degree. A rate is not the person.

Ramadan and Eid in Muslim rooms. Political commemorations some families name and some refuse — 1974, 1991, Tigray, Oromo protest years. Do not collect them as a risk score. Do not referee.

blocks.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023), among those 25 and older in the Ethiopian umbrella: about 81.5 percent high school or higher; about 24.6 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. About 61.7 percent of the community is foreign-born. A large share of children are U.S.-born and in English-dominant schools. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

School and language

A parent who reads fidel, Qubee, or Tigrinya and limited English is not illiterate. Confirm the home language. An Oromo parent is the wrong form if you only brought Amharic. A Tigrayan elder is the wrong form if you booked “Ethiopian.”

Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room that treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of language access plus a school that never learned the name. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter. The child is not the interpreter.

Elders first. Shoes off in many homes. Accept a little food if offered and if they are not fasting. Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time.

In the home

Right hand for food in some rooms. Do not photograph an iconostasis, an altar, or a family and call it rapport. Do not enter a prayer space as a tour. Do not ask an elder to explain Orthodox fasting as entertainment.

Book the language this household names. Amharic is a Semitic language written in fidel. Afaan Oromoo is Cushitic; varieties include Borana, Guji, Wollo, and others — confirm. Tigrinya is not Amharic. An interpreter labeled Ethiopian who speaks Amharic is often a closed door. A Somali interpreter is the wrong door. Arabic may be religion, not the interview.

A long answer may be story. Oral prestige is real in more than one of these peoples. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan.

blocks.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

Named harms

Intra-Ethiopian tension in Minnesota rooms is real — Oromo, Amhara, Tigrayan, and the state’s name itself. Do not pick a side as DHS. Do not referee in a waiver meeting. Do not file politics as a risk score. The 2020–2022 war in Tigray is current structure for some households. Listen if they name it.

FGC exists in some Horn communities. Minnesota law stands. This is not the Somali page. Do not invent an Ethiopian rate. Do not mash Somali prevalence onto this household. Follow mandated reporting. Still see a family.

Colorism and highland/lowland hierarchy sit in some rooms. You do not fix them as a personality. You do not ignore them when they become a gate.

Queer and trans Ethiopian Minnesotans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

Enforcement climate is structure for some. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

Hepatitis B screening for people born in Ethiopia is a U.S. public-health pattern — CDC has treated Ethiopia as a higher-prevalence birth country in screening guidance. Date the CDC page you cite. Do not invent a Minnesota rate. Do not skip screening because the person looks well.

Compass disability 5.4 percent — umbrella, dated. Fasting and medication interact. Ask before you write noncompliance. Mental-health stigma is real in some families. War trauma, depression, and somatic presentation exist. A smile is not a PHQ-9.

No dated Ethiopian-specific Minnesota autism rate belongs on this page. Do not invent one. Do not mash MDH Somali findings onto this umbrella. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. FGC: Minnesota law stands; do not invent a rate; do not skip care. Traditional medicine often sits beside biomedicine. Ask. Co-create. Do not skip a child-protection duty when the facts are the facts.

Imperial incorporation, 1974, the Red Terror, the Derg, the 1980s famine, 1991, the Oromo Liberation struggle as literacy for the desk not a speech, unrest in the 2010s–2020s, and the 2020–2022 war in Tigray — that is the political event. The badge

A DHS badge is not automatically help. Do not use 1974 or Tigray as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate prison, famine, or killing for your professional development.

Enforcement climate in the United States is a different state and still a closed door for some. It changes who opens the door, who signs, and who will not put a relative’s name on a form. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not collect political speech as a risk score.

Restaurant, parking, care work, factory, professional second generation, public employment. Compass median household income about $57,106; poverty 13.0 percent; renter 65.3 percent — umbrella, dated. A rate is not the person. Markets and injera houses are economy and culture. A food-court visit is not consultation.

Work

blocks.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: an interpreter labeled Ethiopian who speaks Amharic is often a closed door for Oromo and Tigrayan households. A Somali interpreter is the wrong door. Confirm the home language and the variety. Still book a qualified interpreter. Do not use a child. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: given name plus father’s name. The database that invents a last name, or that assumes three Somali names, is a gate that follows the person.

Fasting: Wednesday, Friday, Lent, Advent, other seasons for many Orthodox households. Medication with food, labs, morning appointments. Ask. “No-show” may be the feast you scheduled against.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral.

Child welfare and disability: help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole umbrella as a risk score. FGC: Minnesota law stands; this is not the Somali page; do not invent a rate.

Intra-Ethiopian politics: do not pick a side. Do not referee the Tigray war in a waiver meeting.

Deportation climate: people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater. Greater Minnesota is 10.6 percent — a Minneapolis meeting is not the whole channel. SOS already prints Amharic for voters — the packet can print the language this household reads.

Workforce: Ethiopian-identified staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat them.

Somali mash and Black mash: opening Somali because the Horn, or historic African American because both are Black, is a closed door.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that heard “Ethiopian” and booked Somali.

This is a compact learning path built from the full Filipino Minnesota cultural intelligence brief. Use the evidence as a starting hypothesis, not a script. The person or household in front of you is still the authority on their own life.

  • Open this brief when the household is Filipino. Book the language they name. A Spanish surname is not a Latino file.
  • Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity. Practitioner-based means Tuesday: book Tagalog / Filipino or Cebuano or Ilocano or the language they name — not “Asian”; do not mash with Chinese, Hmong, or Vietnamese; no harvesting Filipino staff; Spanish surnames that are not Latino as a file. Employee groups may fact-check. They do not veto U.S. colonial history, model-minority skip, or LEP elders because a Minimization room is uncomfortable.
  • Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Filipino ancestry near 25,203. About 73.5 percent Twin Cities, 26.5 percent Greater Minnesota. About 29.9 percent age 17 or younger; 65+ about 5.1 percent. Foreign-born about 38.4 percent. English only (5+) about 59.6 percent; language other than English about 40.4 percent; English less than “very well” about 8.4 percent. High school or higher (25+) about 92.3 percent; bachelor’s or higher about 53.8 percent. Median household income about $95,275 in 2022 dollars. Poverty 7.3 percent. Owner-occupied about 62.0 percent. Average household size about 2.74. Date Compass. Do not invent other rates. 8.4 percent LEP is not “no language gate.”
  • Nothing from the depth this program requires was kept at full depth. This copy is a living candidate: staff keep a stable doorway until you or an Equity Director in the administration promote.

blocks.body:
This brief is about Filipino people as a people of the Philippines — Luzon, Visayas, Mindanao, many languages — and as a Minnesota community Compass counts near 25,203 (ACS 2019–2023). This is not Chinese. It is not Hmong. It is not Vietnamese. Colonial history is Spanish and then United States, not a China mash. Shared continent is not shared culture. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

Who this is

Tagalog / Filipino is a language, not the only language. Cebuano, Ilocano, and others live in this state. English is official in the Philippines. That fact will be used to skip 8.4 percent LEP. That skip is the gate. Book THIS language. An interpreter labeled Asian is a closed door.

Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 25,203; Twin Cities 73.5 percent; Greater Minnesota 26.5 percent; age 17 or younger 29.9 percent; 65+ about 5.1 percent; foreign-born 38.4 percent; among those 5 and older, English only about 59.6 percent, language other than English about 40.4 percent, English less than “very well” about 8.4 percent; high school or higher (25+) about 92.3 percent; bachelor’s or higher about 53.8 percent; median household income about $95,275 in 2022 dollars; poverty 7.3 percent; owner-occupied 62.0 percent; average household size about 2.74; individuals living alone about 23.6 percent. Female about 58.6 percent — a labor fact in a nursing and care stream, not a personality. Date the number you use.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A U.S.-trained nurse in a Greater Minnesota hospital, a Tagalog-speaking lola who does not read the English IEP, a Cebuano household, an Iglesia ni Cristo family, a Catholic parish household, a U.S.-born student, a person who left during martial law and still will not talk about it in a lobby — share a Compass row and do not share a Tuesday.

How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

blocks.body:
Filipino peoplehood is older than Magellan, older than 1898, and older than the nursing file. Many ethnolinguistic peoples — Tagalog, Cebuano, Ilocano, Kapampangan, Waray, Bikol, and others — and a modern republic named after a Spanish king. That sentence is literacy for the desk. It is not a lecture you give a parent who came in for a waiver.

History for the meeting

Spanish colonial rule, Catholic mission, and then the 1898 war in which the United States took the islands from Spain and fought a Philippine republic — that is the colonial stack. It is not a China mash. It is not the Latino CI because the surnames are Spanish. 4 July 1946 independence is a date. 12 June is the date many Filipino Americans mark. Ask. Do not speech.

What people brought

Baybayin is history. Ordinary public literacy now is Latin script in Tagalog / Filipino, English, and regional languages. Many elders read Tagalog. Some do not. Second generation may not read it at all. English official in the sending country is not a skip of the parent who still cannot run the IEP.

What people brought: a language that may not be Tagalog, Catholic or Iglesia or Protestant or Muslim or none, family obligation, English as a school language, foodways, a memory of occupation and of a state. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, and often an assumption that English official means you can skip the interpreter.

The Philippines is Luzon, the Visayas, Mindanao, and more than seven thousand islands. Manila is not the map. Language shifts. Muslim Mindanao is a named geography some families will name and some will not. You do not referee. Listen if they name a place.

Homeland

The diaspora is global and labor-shaped: United States, Canada, the Gulf, Hong Kong, Singapore, Europe. Overseas Filipino Worker is a sending-country category, not a personality. California, Hawaii, New York, and Illinois hold large U.S. communities. Minnesota is a present.

Minnesota

Compass: about 73.5 percent Twin Cities, 26.5 percent Greater Minnesota. Health-system towns, first-ring suburbs, and Minneapolis–Saint Paul are all on this page. Greater Minnesota is not an afterthought. Do not assume they have been to Manila. A nurse in a southern Minnesota hospital is still this people.

blocks.body:
Spanish colonial rule, then the 1898 U.S. war and occupation, then the Commonwealth, then independence in 1946. U.S. Navy enlistment, bases, and pension streams moved people. Hart-Celler (1965) opened skilled and family immigration. The U.S. nursing and health-care pipeline is a documented Filipino labor pattern. It is work. It is not a personality, not a joke, and not the whole community.

Foundational events

Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos (declared 1972) and the 1986 People Power / EDSA uprising are literacy for the desk. They are not a speech you give the family. They are not an icebreaker. Later: family reunification, students, and ordinary immigration. The desk in 2026 meets U.S.-born children who still cannot get Tagalog for a lola.

Who you meet

If you only know “nurse,” you will miss the elder who needs an interpreter, the Greater Minnesota household far from a parish that speaks the language, and the person whose English is excellent and whose parent’s is not.

Martial-law years and later streams do not share a Tuesday. Compass foreign-born 38.4 percent means a large second generation was born here. They are still this people. The lola is still this people. Do not skip the page because the nurse in the room sounds like Minnesota.

Utang na loob — a debt of gratitude — and bayanihan — mutual aid — are hypotheses in scholarship and in some households. They are not a waiver design and not an excuse to dump remittance, elder care, and a second job onto a daughter.

Who is in the household

Who speaks

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child with the best English. That child is not the qualified interpreter. Using a child as the go-between is a closed door and a harm. Book the interpreter.

Minnesota law still stands. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. Who holds the child’s medical decision may not match the English form. Ask.

blocks.body:
Spanish surnames are Filipino history: Santos, Cruz, Reyes, Garcia, Ramos, de la Cruz, Mendoza. They are not a Latino file. Do not run a Mexican or Puerto Rican script because the last name looks Spanish. Do not mash with the Latino CI. Open that CI when the household is that household.

How to file

Multiple given names and a mother’s family name in Philippine records can collide with a U.S. form that wants one first, one last. The same person can appear as Maria Santos, Maria Cruz Santos, and Maria C. Santos. That is a system failure, not a fraud signal until you have a reason.

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Nicknames are ordinary. Do not treat unmatched names as fraud. Women may or may not take a husband’s name in U.S. records. Mother and child may not match.

blocks.body:
To be Filipino in Minnesota is often to be filed under a checkbox that also holds Chinese, Hmong, and Vietnamese histories this household does not share — and to be asked, in the same week, whether the Spanish surname means Mexican, as if Santos were a Latino file, or whether they “speak Asian.”

In this state

Kapwa — a shared personhood some people name — is a hypothesis, not an icebreaker. Face, hiya, and not shaming the family travel into some waiver meetings. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

Model-minority is a weapon. English official in the Philippines, 53.8 percent bachelor’s, and a nursing pipeline will be used to skip 8.4 percent LEP, 7.3 percent poverty, disability, and the lola who does not read the IEP. That skip is the policy.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization.

blocks.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

Named harms

Model-minority is a weapon. English official, 53.8 percent bachelor’s, and a nursing pipeline will be used to skip 8.4 percent LEP, 7.3 percent poverty, disability, and the lola who does not read the IEP. That skip is the policy.

U.S. colonial amnesia is a building problem. 1898 and occupation are literacy. They are not a speech. They are a reason a government badge is not automatically help.

Remittance labor is work, not a personality. Martial-law memory still sits in some rooms. You do not icebreak with it. You do not put it on a case note as color.

LGBTQ Filipino Minnesotans exist. Undocumented and visa-overstay households exist. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

Mental-health stigma is real in some families. Naming a counselor is not the same as a family accepting one. A smile is not a PHQ-9. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it.

Hilot, herbs, and parish prayer often sit beside biomedicine. Ask. Co-create. Do not mock. Do not skip a child-protection duty when the facts are the facts. A Filipino nurse on staff is not the interpreter and not the culture unit.

Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Filipino cultural community: about 25,203; Twin Cities 73.5%; Greater Minnesota 26.5%; age 17 or younger 29.9%; 65+ about 5.1%; foreign-born 38.4%; English only (age 5+) 59.6%; language other than English 40.4%; English less than “very well” 8.4%; high school or higher (25+) 92.3%; bachelor’s or higher 53.8%; median household income about $95,275 (2022 dollars); poverty 7.3%; owner-occupied 62.0%; average household size 2.74; individuals living alone 23.6 percent. Female about 58.6 percent.

Counts

Date Compass. Do not invent other rates. Counts disagree across ACS vintages and definitions. Date the number you cite.

What the count is not

An 8.4 percent LEP rate is not zero. A 7.3 percent poverty rate is not zero. Greater Minnesota 26.5 percent is not an afterthought. English official in the Philippines is not a skip. A rate is not the person.

blocks.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: 8.4 percent LEP is not “no language gate.” English official in the Philippines is not a skip. An elder who needs Tagalog or Cebuano and gets English — or “Asian” — is a closed door. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Do not use a child.

Names: Spanish surnames are Filipino history. The database that files Santos as Latino, or flattens three given names, is a gate.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without this household’s language are not culturally neutral. An English IEP is still a gate for that parent.

Model-minority: 92.3 percent high school, 53.8 percent bachelor’s, and a nursing pipeline will be used to skip LEP, 7.3 percent poverty, disability, and the lola. That skip is the policy.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how an LEP elder was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater. Greater Minnesota is 26.5 percent — a Minneapolis meeting is not the whole channel.

Workforce: Filipino staff are not the interpreter pool. A nurse is not the culture unit. Neither is the community.

Asian mash: opening Chinese or Hmong or Vietnamese because the checkbox says Asian is a closed door. Latino mash on a Spanish surname is a closed door.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that never learned that English official is still a door, and that Filipino is not Chinese.
