This is a compact learning path built from the full Oromo Minnesota cultural intelligence brief. Use the evidence as a starting hypothesis, not a script. The person or household in front of you is still the authority on their own life.

  • Open this brief when the household is Oromo. Book Afaan Oromoo if that is the language. An “Ethiopian interpreter” can still be the wrong door.
  • Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity. Practitioner-based means Tuesday: Afaan Oromoo on the interpreter line, not Amharic, not Somali, not “Ethiopian”; names that are not Amharic and not three Somali names; no harvesting Oromo staff; follow this room on greeting and faith. Employee groups may fact-check. They do not veto Qubee, intra-Ethiopian tension, or child-welfare fear because a Minimization room is uncomfortable.
  • Counts disagree. Compass Ethiopian Minnesota (ACS 2019–2023) near 40,324 is an umbrella — Amhara, Oromo, Tigrayan and others are not one file. MinnPost 19 May 2016: OCIM estimated up to 40,000 Oromo in Minnesota; the state demographer nearer 8,500 using census plus school language. Star Tribune 31 July 2025: about 8,000 Minnesotans speak Oromo at home; MDE: Oromo 8th most-common home language in K–12. Date the disagreement. A rate is not the person.
  • Nothing from the depth this program requires was kept at full depth. This copy is a living candidate: staff keep a stable doorway until you or an Equity Director in the administration promote.

blocks.body:
This brief is about Oromo people — Oromoo; the language Afaan Oromoo — as a Cushitic-speaking nation of the Horn and as a Minnesota community. Oromo is not Somali. Not Amharic. Not “Ethiopian” as a synonym. If you open Somali Minnesota or book an Amharic interpreter because the building heard East Africa, you have already closed the door.

Who this is

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Ethiopian Minnesota near 40,324: 89.4 percent Twin Cities, 10.6 percent Greater Minnesota; 43.5 percent age 17 or younger; 61.7 percent foreign-born; language other than English (age 5+) 74.9 percent; LEP 30.4 percent. Compass note historically: respondents born in Ethiopia who list Somali ancestry are counted Somali, not Ethiopian. Ethiopian Compass is an umbrella — Amhara, Oromo, Tigrayan and others are not one file. Use Ethiopian numbers as dated context, not as an Oromo census.

Who this is not

Oromo-specific counts disagree. MinnPost (19 May 2016): the Oromo Community of Minnesota estimated up to 40,000 Oromo in the state; the state demographer’s office nearer 8,500 using census plus school language. Star Tribune (31 July 2025): about 8,000 Minnesotans speak Oromo at home; Minnesota Department of Education: Oromo was the 8th most-common home language in K–12. Date the disagreement. Do not invent a midpoint. A rate is not the person.

How to read this

Islam and Christianity (Orthodox, Protestant) and Waaqeffanna traditional practice all live here. Do not assume Muslim like Somali. Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

blocks.body:
Oromo peoplehood — Oromummaa — is older than the Ethiopian empire’s file on it and older than the refugee camp. Oromo people are a Cushitic-speaking nation of the Horn, the largest nation in the region by language. There is no Oromo nation-state. Gadaa (generational / governance tradition) is literacy for the desk, not a speech you give the family, and not every household still lives it.

History for the meeting

Afaan Oromoo is not Amharic. Amharic is a Semitic language and was the imperial state language. Latin Qubee script, adopted in the early 1990s after the fall of the Derg, is political and educational history: a people writing itself after suppression. That sentence is literacy. It is not a lecture in the lobby.

What people brought

What people brought: language and dialect, Islam and Christianity and Waaqeffanna, kinship, oral art, a memory of imperial and 20th-century state violence. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Ethiopian” checkbox, one “East African” interpreter, and often Somali because the building already has that page.

Do not assume Addis Ababa as identity. Many Oromo people name Oromia, a region, a village, a lineage — not the capital of the state that ruled them.

Homeland is Oromia and Oromo-inhabited country across the Horn — a map that does not match the Ethiopian state’s ethnic-federal drawing in every family’s mouth. Oromo communities also live in Kenya. A global diaspora: Middle East, Europe, North America. After Kenya, Minnesota has been named among the largest Oromo communities outside the homeland (MNHS / MNopedia). Twin Cities as Little Oromia is community naming, not a census.

Homeland

Compass Ethiopian (ACS 2019–2023): 89.4 percent Twin Cities, 10.6 percent Greater Minnesota — umbrella, not an Oromo map. Do not assume Cedar-Riverside. That sentence is Somali geography unless this family lives there. Do not assume Addis.

Minnesota

Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Oromia. Secondary migration built parts of this map. Greater Minnesota is still this people when they live there.

blocks.body:
There is no single 1975 or 1991 on this page. The foundational political literacy is longer: Ethiopian imperial incorporation of Oromo country, 20th-century state violence, the Oromo Liberation struggle as literacy for the desk not a speech, the 1974 revolution and the Derg, flight through Sudan and Kenya and the Gulf, U.S. resettlement, secondary migration to Minnesota, and unrest in the 2010s–2020s that sent another wave.

Foundational events

Do not referee Ethiopian politics in a waiver meeting. Do not pick a side as DHS. Intra-Ethiopian tension in Minnesota rooms is real. Listen if they name it. Do not file it as a risk score.

Who you meet

The desk in 2026 meets first-wave elders and U.S.-born children — English-dominant with peers, still translating for parents, still unable to get Afaan Oromoo in a lobby that offered Somali or Amharic.

If you only know “Ethiopian refugee,” you will miss this household.

blocks.body:
Extended households and elder authority sit in many rooms. Compass Ethiopian average household size 3.09 (ACS 2019–2023) is umbrella context, not an Oromo census. Who cares for the child may not match the waiver checkbox. Ask who should be in the room.

Who is in the household

Patronymic patterns exist: given name and father’s name, sometimes more. Do not invent a last name because the screen requires one. Do not assume three Somali names. Oromo names are not Amharic names.

Who speaks

Women’s labor, men’s labor, and church or mosque obligation all live here. Both a nuclear English form and a cousin-line can be true in the same week.

Do not collect status you do not need. Mixed-status fear is structure in some rooms.

blocks.body:
Islam and Christianity both live in Oromo Minnesota in large streams. Orthodox and Protestant (including Oromo evangelical churches) are ordinary. Waaqeffanna — traditional Oromo religious practice — lives in some rooms and as public revival in others. Do not assume Muslim like Somali. Do not assume Orthodox like a mash of “Ethiopian.”

Streams

Arabic may be religion, not the interview. Qurʾanic recitation is not Afaan Oromoo. Book the interview language.

Practice

Do not import As-salāmu ʿalaykum as default. In a Christian Oromo room it is already a closed door. In a Muslim Oromo room it may be ordinary. Follow this room.

Do not make an imam or a pastor the case plan unless this family asked. Halal and fasting matter in some rooms and not in others. Illness meaning may not be the DSM sentence. Ask.

Elders first. Follow this room. Many Christian Oromo. Many Muslim Oromo. As-salāmu ʿalaykum is not default. English hello is ordinary in the second generation. Afaan Oromoo greetings exist — ask, do not perform one you learned from a video.

Titles

A hard handshake you assume is universal is already a closed door for some women and some elders. Many second-generation people will shake hands in English-language rooms. If a hand is not offered, nod. Do not force it.

This room

Do not import the Black nod onto this page. Do not import Somali greeting rules as if Oromo were Somali.

Physical contact: ask the room. Cross-gender touch is not a default in some families.

blocks.body:
Oromo names are not Amharic names. Patronymic patterns exist: given name, father’s name, sometimes grandfather’s. That can look like a Somali three-part name and is not. Do not assume three Somali names. Do not invent a last name because the screen requires one. That invented name becomes a gate.

How to file

Ask how to say it and how to file it. Pronounce it.

Women may or may not take a husband’s name in U.S. records. Ask how to file. Do not “correct” a mother and child who do not share a last name as a fraud signal until you have a reason.

Do not joke about names. Do not collect a clan list as an icebreaker. Clan as Oromo social fact is not the Somali qabiil icebreaker and not a risk score.

blocks.body:
This department will meet this community on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment. Twin Cities as Little Oromia is community memory (MNHS / MNopedia), not a Compass line. Greater Minnesota exists.

Places

Partners: Oromo Community of Minnesota (OCIM / OCM) historically, from the 1980s. Churches and mosques families name — including Our Redeemer Oromo Evangelical Church (from a 1980s Bible study, organized 1993 per MNHS) and Tawfiq Islamic Center in Minneapolis (MNHS: first Oromo mosque in North America, opened 2004 as Masjid Tawfiq). Pay. Report back. CECLC is a door, not the whole.

Partners

Oromo staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. A festival or Irreecha visit is optional professional development. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

blocks.body:
To be Oromo in Minnesota is to be a Cushitic nation without a state, filed under Ethiopian, East African, Black, and sometimes Somali by a building that has not studied. Oromummaa is peoplehood. It is not a poster. Islam, Orthodox and Protestant Christianity, and Waaqeffanna all live here. Do not assume the mosque.

In this state

Many Oromo Minnesotans are Black in a U.S. racial order that also holds Somali and historic African American histories they do not share. Shared race is not shared culture. Shared Horn geography is not shared language.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Ask this household.

Faith is plural

blocks.body:
Qubee in the 1990s is why a mass written Afaan Oromoo public exists. That is political history and school history. Many elders still do not read it. Many children in Minnesota schools do. The English IEP still has to reach the parent.

School and language

Compass Ethiopian (ACS 2019–2023), among those 25 and older: about 81.5 percent high school or higher; about 24.6 percent bachelor’s or higher — umbrella, not an Oromo census. Star Tribune (31 July 2025): MDE listed Oromo as the 8th most-common home language in K–12. Date it.

A parent who speaks fluent Afaan Oromoo and limited English is not illiterate. The child is not the interpreter. Book Oromo, not Amharic. An English-only form is the gate.

blocks.body:
Elders first. Hospitality is a virtue in many rooms. Accept a little tea if offered. You still keep medical and legal time.

In the home

Shoes off in some homes. Faith practice varies — mosque, Orthodox liturgy, Protestant church, Waaqeffanna, none. Follow this room. Do not rank covering. Do not assume covering.

Time

Do not photograph a family and call it rapport. Do not enter a prayer space as a tour.

On-time for appointments. Multi-household logistics are real. So is a courtesy-yes then no-show when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in Afaan Oromoo if that is the language they use.

blocks.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

Named harms

Intra-Ethiopian tension in Minnesota rooms is real — Oromo, Amhara, Tigrayan, and the state’s name itself. Do not pick a side as DHS. Do not referee in a waiver meeting. Do not file politics as a risk score.

FGC exists in some Horn communities. Minnesota law stands. This is not the Somali page. Do not invent an Oromo rate. Do not mash Somali prevalence onto this household. Follow mandated reporting. Still see a family.

Queer and trans Oromo exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture.

Enforcement climate is structure for some. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance.

Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Ethiopian cultural community — umbrella, not an Oromo census: about 40,324; Twin Cities 89.4%; Greater Minnesota 10.6%; age 17 or younger 43.5%; 65+ 3.6%; foreign-born 61.7%; language other than English (age 5+) 74.9%; English less than “very well” 30.4%; high school or higher (25+) 81.5%; bachelor’s or higher 24.6%; median household income about $57,106 (2022 dollars, averaged); poverty 13.0%; owner-occupied 34.7%; renter-occupied 65.3%; average household size 3.09. Compass: respondents born in Ethiopia who list Somali ancestry are counted Somali, not Ethiopian.

Counts

Oromo-specific counts disagree. MinnPost, 19 May 2016: OCIM estimated up to 40,000 Oromo in Minnesota; state demographer nearer 8,500 using census plus school language. Star Tribune, 31 July 2025: about 8,000 Minnesotans speak Oromo at home; MDE: Oromo 8th most-common home language in K–12.

What the count is not

blocks.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: Oromo versus Amharic versus Somali mash is the first failure. An interpreter labeled Ethiopian who speaks Amharic is often a closed door. A Somali interpreter is the wrong door. Arabic may be religion, not the interview. Confirm the variety (Borana, Guji, Wollo, others). Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: Oromo names are not Amharic names. The database that invents a last name, or that assumes three Somali names, is a gate that follows the person.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral.

Child welfare: help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole community as a risk score. FGC: Minnesota law stands; this is not the Somali page; do not invent a rate.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater.

Workforce: Oromo staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat them.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that filed Oromo under Somali or under Ethiopian as a synonym.

blocks.body:
This is a compact learning path built from the full Puerto Rican Minnesota cultural intelligence brief. Use the evidence as a starting hypothesis, not a script. The person or household in front of you is still the authority on their own life.

  • Open this brief when the household is Puerto Rican. Citizenship is already settled. Ask about language and who should be in the room.
  • Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity. Practitioner-based means Tuesday: origin is Puerto Rican, not Mexican; do not run an immigration script by default; Spanish AND English — ask, do not assume LEP; two surnames still common; no child as interpreter; no harvesting Puerto Rican or Latino staff; Greater Minnesota 32.9 percent is not an afterthought. Employee groups may fact-check. They do not veto colonial status, Hurricane María, Afro-Puerto Rican peoplehood, or the fact that this is citizenship because a Minimization room is uncomfortable. Minnesota Nice deletes facts.
  • Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): 21,802; Twin Cities 67.1 percent; Greater Minnesota 32.9 percent. Age 17 or younger 38.2 percent; 65+ 5.5 percent; foreign-born 1.3 percent; English only (5+) 62.2 percent; language other than English 37.8 percent; English less than very well 10.2 percent; high school or higher (25+) 93.9 percent; bachelor’s or higher 38.6 percent; median household income about $63,141; poverty 12.0 percent; owner 42.0 percent; average household 2.39; disability 12.8 percent. Date Compass. Do not invent other rates.
  • Nothing from the depth this program requires was kept at full depth. This copy is a living candidate: staff keep a stable doorway until you or an Equity Director in the administration promote.
blocks.heading: How to use this guide

blocks.body:
This brief is about Puerto Rican Minnesota as a people — boricua, puertorriqueño, puertorriqueña — not as a Mexican variant, not as an immigrant file, and not as the Latino / Hispanic umbrella. U.S. citizens since the Jones Act (2 March 1917). Do not run an immigration script by default. Compass foreign-born is 1.3 percent because ACS does not count birth on the island as foreign. Spanish varieties exist. English-dominant households exist. This is not Mexican. It is not Guatemalan. It is not Salvadoran. Shared Spanish is not shared culture. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

Who this is

Open the Latino umbrella only as adjacent. That page is the mash and the CLAS Spanish line. This page is Puerto Rican. If you leave this door and file the household under “Latino” or under Mexican, or greet them with an ICE speech because the name is Spanish, you have left this door.

Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts the Puerto Rican cultural community at 21,802. Twin Cities 67.1 percent; Greater Minnesota 32.9 percent — not an afterthought. About 38.2 percent age 17 or younger; 5.5 percent 65+. English only (age 5+) 62.2 percent; language other than English 37.8 percent; English less than “very well” 10.2 percent. Date the number you use. LEP 10.2 percent is not “no language gate.” A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. An island-born elder who uses Spanish, a Minnesota-born English-dominant kid, a Nuyorican household that moved west, a person displaced after Hurricane María, an Afro-Puerto Rican student, a Greater Minnesota worker the building filed as Mexican, a queer second-generation adult who uses English with friends and Spanish with a grandmother — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

blocks.body:
Puerto Rican peoplehood is older than 1917 and older than the Minnesota file. Borikén. Taíno people, Spanish colonial rule, African enslavement in the sugar and later coffee economy — that three-root sentence is literacy for the desk. It is incomplete. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a salsa tourism sentence or a Heritage Month flag.

History for the meeting

1898: the United States took the island in the war with Spain. Colony. The Jones Act (2 March 1917) made Puerto Ricans U.S. citizens. Citizenship without treating the household as foreign is the first operational fact on this desk. They still cannot vote for president from the island. They can, if they reside in Minnesota. That is colonial status as literacy, not a lecture.

What people brought

Spanish and English are both official on the island. Writing in both exists. Some elders read Spanish and not English. Some Minnesota-born adults read English and not Spanish. Some read both. Ask. Oral skill is not print.

What people brought: language (Caribbean Spanish and English), kinship, Catholic and later Protestant church, Afro-diasporic practice in some families, baseball, a memory of a colony that claimed them. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Latino” checkbox, often one interpreter labeled Spanish, and a lobby that had already decided they were immigrants.

blocks.body:
Homeland is the island — municipalities people name, San Juan, Ponce, Mayagüez, the mountains, the coast. Vieques and Culebra are not trivia. Confirm the place if they name it. Do not referee San Juan versus the west in a waiver meeting. Listen.

Homeland

The U.S. Puerto Rican map is New York (Nuyorican as a named diaspora), Chicago, Florida, Pennsylvania, and also Minnesota. Those hubs are not this map. Secondary migration, military, school, and work pulled people here. Hurricane María (2017) moved people again.

Minnesota

In Minnesota: Twin Cities 67.1 percent, Greater Minnesota 32.9 percent (Compass ACS 2019–2023). Greater Minnesota is not an afterthought. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to the island. Do not assume a Spanish-surnamed household in a plant town is Mexican. A Greater Minnesota household is still this people.

blocks.body:
This is internal U.S. migration, not immigration. Jones Act, 1917. Operation Bootstrap in the mid-twentieth century pushed industrial policy on the island and labor to the mainland — New York, Chicago, and later other states. Nuyorican is a named diaspora. Minnesota is a later present. Do not run an immigration script by default because the name is Spanish.

Foundational events

Hurricane María (September 2017) is displacement literacy for the desk. People left a wrecked grid. Some came here. That is not an immigrant wave. It is citizens moving inside the United States after a disaster. PROMESA and the fiscal control board are political literacy. They are not a speech you give the family.

Who you meet

The desk in 2026 meets island-born elders, U.S.-mainland-born adults, Minnesota-born children, and mixed island–mainland households. Compass foreign-born 1.3 percent is the ACS fact: birth in Puerto Rico is not foreign-born. If you only know “immigrant,” you will miss them and you will harm them.

Enforcement climate in the wider Latino lobby still spills. A Puerto Rican citizen can still be asked for papers because the building mashed the file. That is the gate. Do not collect status you do not need.

blocks.body:
Kin networks often run island to mainland to Minnesota in the same month. Compass: average household size about 2.39 — smaller than some neighboring spines. Still not always a nuclear English form. Elders, adult children, and cousins who are household in practice sit in the same week. Who cares for a child may not match the waiver checkbox. Ask who should be in the room.

Who is in the household

Do not treat this household as mixed-status by default. Citizenship is the fact. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat unmatched last names or a grandmother as caregiver as fraud until you have a reason. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

Who speaks

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child. Even in an English-dominant household, a child is not the qualified interpreter for a Spanish-speaking elder — and an English-speaking adult is not a child to be skipped. CLAS still stands when Spanish is needed. Using a child as the go-between is a harm.

Minnesota law still stands. Domestic violence is not culture. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

blocks.body:
Catholic majority in many streams — not all. Protestant and evangelical churches live here. Espiritismo and Santería live in some families. Do not exoticize. Do not assume. Do not treat Afro-diasporic practice as folklore or as a risk note. Our Lady of Guadalupe is Mexican Catholic literacy. Do not install it as the default on this page. Ask.

Streams

Do not make a priest or a pastor the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one parish and call it consultation.

Practice

Three Kings (6 January) is larger than Santa in some rooms. Holy Week, funerals, and family obligation can collide with your calendar. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it. Do not photograph an altar.

Help that looks like a report is not help. Religious framing of disability, mental health, or gender can sit next to a fierce wish for services. You can hold both.

blocks.body:
Elders first. A handshake is common in many rooms. Many English-dominant second-generation rooms will move to a first name faster than a Mexican Spanish room. Follow this room. Do not force a first name on an elder because the form printed it.

Titles

Titles — Señor, Señora, Don, Doña — until invited in some Spanish rooms. English “hello” is ordinary in others. Say the name. There may be two surnames. Do not assume a Spanish greeting is required, and do not assume English is a closed door to Spanish.

This room

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars. Cross-gender touch: follow this room. A hug from staff is not warmth if the household did not offer it.

blocks.body:
Two surnames remain common: apellido paterno then apellido materno. A U.S. database that keeps one surname invents a person. That invented name then follows them through MHCP, child welfare, and school. It is a gate.

How to file

English-style single last names exist in some U.S.-born and some mainland-raised households. Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Do not drop accents as a joke. Given names may be Spanish, English, or both. Some people use a middle given name as the call-name.

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default. Do not invent a hyphen and then punish the person when the hyphen moves.

blocks.body:
Minnesota holds a Puerto Rican community large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment. Compass: 21,802 (ACS 2019–2023). Twin Cities 67.1 percent; Greater Minnesota 32.9 percent — not an afterthought. Do not write this people as a New York anecdote and do not write them as a Mexican leftover.

Places

Places, not a blob: Twin Cities corridors and suburbs; Greater Minnesota towns with work, school, and military ties. Public culture is not a sombrero mash. A festival visit does not make you the expert.

Partners

Partners: parishes and cultural groups families name; rural partners when the household is Greater Minnesota — name the local one; do not assume Minneapolis. CLUES is a Twin Cities Latino door, adjacent, not automatic reach and not this people. CECLC is a department door, not the community. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Puerto Rican staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. You are a guest at a public event if invited. It does not make you the expert.

blocks.body:
To be Puerto Rican in Minnesota is to be a people with an island, a colony, and U.S. citizenship, filed under a checkbox that defaults Mexican and often immigrant. Face, kin, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

In this state

Afro-Puerto Rican people exist. Colorism is real. Do not bleach this household into a mestizo Latino story, and do not mash them into historic African American because both are Black. Ask.

The Mexican default in this state is a count fact on another page. It is a harm on this one when staff copy Guadalupe, ICE, and “the interpreter” onto a citizen household that may be English-dominant.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.

Spanish and English both

The database that keeps one invents a person. English-style single last names exist in some U.S.-born households. Ask.

Afro-Puerto Rican peoplehood

Not a footnote. Not the African American CI as the file.

Colonial status

Literacy for the desk. Not a speech you give the family. María (2017) is displacement, not an immigrant wave.

blocks.body:
6 January — Día de los Reyes / Three Kings. Larger than Santa in some Puerto Rican rooms. Literacy for scheduling. Not a costume for staff.

Calendar

25 July is contested public memory: 1898 U.S. landing, and Constitution Day of the commonwealth. 19 November is marked in some public life. You do not referee independence versus commonwealth versus statehood on a case note. Listen if they name a day.

Hurricane María — September 2017 — is displacement literacy, not a holiday. Hispanic Heritage Month is the umbrella calendar. It is not this people’s day and not consultation. Not Cinco de Mayo. Not Mexican 16 September. Do not put “Latino holiday” on a case note. A calendar click is not community engagement and not a day off the work.

blocks.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Puerto Rican Minnesotans 25 and older, about 93.9 percent high school or higher; about 38.6 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. Do not invent a dropout rate. English only (age 5+) 62.2 percent. LEP 10.2 percent is not “no language gate.” The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it — in English or in Spanish.

School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Caribbean Spanish and limited English is not illiterate. A parent who is English-dominant is not “no culture” and not proof the elder in the household needs no interpreter. Ask. Do not use a child as interpreter.

Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room that treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of a school that never learned the second surname, or that filed this student as “immigrant.” Puerto Rican students are not immigrant students by default. Do not collect status you do not need at enrollment theater.

Time

On-time for appointments. Social time can run long. Work, clinic, and court time should be treated as on time. Do not write a “Latino time” joke in a case note.

blocks.body:
Salsa, bomba, plena, reggaeton, church music. Named variation, not a playlist. A Mexican mariachi default in this waiting room is the mash in speakers.

Variation

A festival stage is not engagement. A playlist is not language access. Bomba and plena are public culture and Afro-diasporic literacy, not staff entertainment.

Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

Named harms

Do not run an immigration script by default. Citizenship since 1917. Foreign-born 1.3 percent. SSN theater on the first screen is a gate even for a citizen when the building mashed Latino into ICE. Do not collect status you do not need.

The Mexican default in this state will talk over this household if you let the umbrella page do this page’s job. Colorism is real. Afro-Puerto Rican erasure under a mestizo Latino story is a named harm. Do not mash Afro-Puerto Rican people into the historic African American CI because both are Black, and do not bleach them.

Colonial status is structure: PROMESA, the board, María, the grid. It is not a personality. Machismo is a named harm, not a joke and not “that’s culture.” Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. You still see a family.

LGBTQ Puerto Rican Minnesotans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: ask. English-dominant households exist. Caribbean Spanish is not Mexican Spanish. CLAS Spanish is not one Spanish. LEP 10.2 percent (Compass ACS 2019–2023) is not zero. Still book a qualified interpreter when they need one. Do not use a child. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: two surnames still common. The database that keeps one invents a person. Unmatched last names are not fraud by default.

Citizenship: Jones Act 1917. Do not run an immigration script by default. SSN theater on the first screen is a gate when the building mashed Latino into ICE. Do not collect status you do not need.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without asking language are not culturally neutral.

Child welfare and disability: Compass disability 12.8 percent — date it. Help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole community as a risk score. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow law.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached if the elder reads Spanish — and an English PDF is not automatically wrong if the household is English-dominant. Ask. Empty follow-up cells are theater. Greater Minnesota is 32.9 percent — a St. Paul meeting is not the whole channel.

Workforce: Puerto Rican staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat them.

Latino mash: opening Mexican, or the umbrella, because the checkbox says Hispanic is a closed door. Opening an ICE script is a closed door.

This is a compact learning path built from the full Russian-speaking Minnesota cultural intelligence brief. Use the evidence as a starting hypothesis, not a script. The person or household in front of you is still the authority on their own life.

  • Open this brief when Russian may be the language. Confirm whether it is actually the home language. Ukrainian Minnesota is a different brief.
  • Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity — and refusing to invent a community population where Compass has no Russian cultural-community profile. Practitioner-based means Tuesday: book a qualified Russian interpreter; do not treat Ukrainian; put the patronymic on the form; do not assume English because the person is white; do not harvest Russian-speaking staff as the interpreter or the community. Employee groups may fact-check. They do not veto Ukraine-war structure, alcohol and family violence as facts, or queer people in this language because a Minimization room is uncomfortable.
  • There is no Compass “Russian Minnesota” people-count. Compass immigration table: about 6,483 foreign-born from Russia — date the table; that is not speakers. Compass Ukrainian cultural community is about 22,570 (ACS 2019–2023) — do not mash it into this door. Star Tribune 2025: Russian is among languages each representing about 2% of Minnesotans who speak a language other than English at home. SOS voter materials include Russian. Date the number. Do not invent the rest.
  • Nothing from the depth this program requires was kept at full depth. This copy is a living candidate: staff keep a stable doorway until you or an Equity Director in the administration promote.
blocks.heading: How to use this guide

blocks.body:
This brief is about Russian as a language door on the department’s CLAS five-language standing written list — with Hmong, Somali, Spanish, and Vietnamese — not as one people. If you invent a single “Russian community” from that list, you have already left this door. A list is not the person and not the dialect. Still book a qualified interpreter.

Who this is

Disaggregate before you open a file. Ethnic Russians. Soviet Jews of the 1970s–90s refusenik / Jackson-Vanik stream. Ukrainian households who use Russian — not the Ukrainian people-page; Compass Ukrainian is about 22,570 (ACS 2019–2023); do not mash. Belarusian, Central Asian, and Caucasian Russian-speakers. Evangelical and Baptist Russians, including some Greater Minnesota towns. Recent arrivals versus 1990s versus a third generation that may not need you to speak Russian at all.

Who this is not

A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Shared language is not shared origin, not shared religion, and not shared politics. The Ukraine war is current structure for some households and a trap if you assume every Russian speaker is a combatant or a Putin voter.

There is no Minnesota Compass cultural-community profile titled Russian. Compass immigration table: about 6,483 foreign-born from Russia — date the table you open; that is not a count of speakers. ACS language-at-home figures disagree across vintages. Star Tribune (31 July 2025): Russian is among languages each representing about 2% of Minnesotans who speak a language other than English at home. Minnesota Secretary of State voter materials include Russian. Date the number. Do not invent a community population.

The diversity inside this language is the point. A Jewish grandmother who left on an exit visa in 1989, an Orthodox parishioner, a Belarusian family that uses Russian at the table, a Ukrainian household that will not accept a “former Soviet” interpreter after 2022, a Baptist family in a Greater Minnesota town, a professional who does not need an interpreter and whose elder does — share a language on a form and do not share a Tuesday.

How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this household.

blocks.body:
There is no single founding of “Russian-speaking Minnesota.” Ethnic Russian peoplehood is older than the Soviet Union and older than this department. It is not the whole door. Other peoples used Russian as an imperial and Soviet language of school, army, and office. That history is why a language list is not a census of who counts.

History for the meeting

Late-imperial emigration included Jews fleeing pogroms and others leaving the Russian Empire. Some of that older Jewish Minnesota is English-dominant now and is not this CLAS door. Do not mash a 1910 synagogue story onto a 1994 arrival and call it one community.

What people brought

The Soviet period produced later streams: dissidents, Jews denied exit (refuseniks) until Jackson-Vanik and the years that followed opened a way, and then the 1991 collapse of the USSR, which moved people for work, family, and survival. Evangelical Protestants — Baptists and related churches — left in named waves as well. Central Asian and Caucasian families may carry Russian as a public language beside another home language.

What people brought is not one kit: Orthodox practice, Jewish peoplehood, evangelical church, Soviet official atheism, Cyrillic literacy, professional skill the U.S. did not always recognize, and a memory of a state that surveilled. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, a racial order that may file them as white and skip the interpreter, and often one interpreter labeled “Russian.”

Homeland is not one flag. The Russian Federation is a geography some families name. Ukraine is another — and a Ukrainian household that uses Russian is still not this page’s invented people. Belarus, Kazakhstan and other Central Asian states, the Caucasus, the Baltics: Russian as a Soviet-era public language still sits in some of those rooms. Do not referee borders in a waiver meeting. Listen if they name a place.

Homeland

The diaspora is global: Israel and Germany for large Jewish streams, the United States, Canada, and Europe. Brighton Beach is not Minnesota. Brooklyn, northern New Jersey, and California sit on a different map. Secondary migration and church networks built some of what you will meet here.

Minnesota

In Minnesota: Twin Cities households; some inner-ring suburbs; Orthodox parishes and synagogues as named places, not a blob; evangelical and Baptist congregations in some towns, including Greater Minnesota. Do not assume Northeast Minneapolis. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Russia. Do not assume a Greater Minnesota town has no Russian-speaking church.

blocks.body:
If 1975 is the foundational event of Hmong Minnesota and 1991 of Somali Minnesota, Russian-speaking Minnesota does not get one year. It gets a stack, and you will misread the room if you pick the wrong one.

Foundational events

Late-imperial flight. Soviet emigration in drips and then in named openings. The 1970s–90s Jewish stream — refuseniks, Jackson-Vanik (1974) as U.S. law tying trade to emigration, then the late-1980s and 1990s movement — built part of Twin Cities Jewish life. That stream is Jewish peoplehood meeting Minnesota synagogues and a JCC, not a nesting-doll exhibit. 1991 and the collapse of the USSR moved others: ethnic Russians, mixed families, professionals, people from republics that were suddenly different countries.

Who you meet

Evangelical and Baptist Russians arrived in church-sponsored patterns that sometimes landed in Greater Minnesota, not only in Minneapolis. Later family and employment streams are ordinary immigration, not a refugee poster.

2022 and the war on Ukraine is current structure for some households in this language: relatives under fire, mixed families, people who will not accept a Russian-language flyer that looks like Moscow. It is a trap if you treat every Russian speaker as a combatant or a Putin voter. It is also a trap if you pretend the war is not in the room when they name it. Literacy for the desk. Not a speech you give the family.

blocks.body:
Family is not one size. Some households look nuclear on an English form and still carry obligation to a parent who does not drive and does not read the form. Some are three generations in one week. Some are a single elder whose children live in another metro. Elder isolation is a named harm in this language door. It is not a cultural virtue.

Who is in the household

The patronymic — a name built from the father — is how a person is fully named in Russian. A form that keeps only first and last has already dropped a who. Ask how to file. Ask who should be in the room.

Who speaks

Adult children may speak for an elder in English. That is a hypothesis, not permission to skip the interpreter or to use a child. CLAS still stands. A sixteen-year-old in the lobby is not the qualified interpreter.

Women’s labor and professional second generation sit next to older gender patterns in some rooms. Both can be true. Minnesota law still stands on violence, neglect, and who may consent. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it culture.

Ask. Do not assume Russian Orthodox because the language is Russian. Russian Orthodox, Jewish, evangelical Protestant, and none all live in this door. Soviet official atheism left a mark in some families that still keep a holiday table.

Streams

The parish is a center of liturgy, memorial, and sometimes mutual aid. It is not the community. Do not BCC one priest and call it consultation. Icons in a home are not a case plan and not a museum.

Practice

Jewish households in the 1970s–90s stream may be secular in the Soviet sense and still Jewish in peoplehood — synagogue, JCC, kosher as a maybe, Hebrew school as a maybe. Do not give them an Orthodox Christian flyer and call it language access. Do not give them a “Russian culture night” and call it Jewish.

Evangelical and Baptist congregations — some in Greater Minnesota — can be the whole public life of a household. Church English and home Russian may sit together. Do not make the pastor the case plan unless they asked.

Do not rank piety. A person who left the church or the synagogue is still this language door if that is the language they need.

blocks.body:
Handshake is common in many rooms — men, and often women in professional space. Follow this room. Some older Orthodox or observant Jewish settings will change the rule. You nod if a hand is not offered. You do not make a scene in the lobby.

Titles

Titles matter. First name plus patronymic is the respectful Russian address for an adult you do not know well. English Mr./Ms. plus family name is a decent substitute if you cannot produce the patronymic. Do not use a first name with an elder because the form printed it.

This room

Zdravstvuyte is the formal hello. English “hello” is ordinary, especially with the second generation. Say the name. Ask how to say it.

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars. Physical contact: follow this person. A hug from staff is not warmth if the household did not offer it.

blocks.body:
A common Russian pattern is given name, patronymic, family name: a person is Ivan Petrovich Sokolov because his father is Petr. Maria Ivanovna Sokolova because her father is Ivan. The patronymic is not a middle name you may drop for convenience. Databases that drop it invent a person. That invented person then fails a match in MHCP, child welfare, and school.

How to file

Family names may take a gendered ending. Sokolov / Sokolova is the same family. The form that flags the difference as fraud has already chosen a household type. Ask how to file. Ask how this person wants the English record to read.

Jewish, Ukrainian, Belarusian, Central Asian, and Caucasian names in this language door will not all look like Ivan and Maria. Do not “correct” a name toward a Russian textbook. Pronounce it. Ask.

The form that demands first-middle-last and a hyphen will invent a person. Do not invent a last name, and do not invent a middle initial from a patronymic without asking. Three people in one household may not share a “last name” the way a Swedish Minnesota form expects. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

blocks.body:
Minnesota put Russian on the CLAS five because the building already knew it would meet this language on notices, health care, cash, food, aging, and voting — not because Compass drew a people-blob titled Russian. That is the honest origin of this spine. A language list is operations. It is not a census.

Places

Places, not a blob: Twin Cities; inner-ring suburbs; some Greater Minnesota towns with evangelical churches. Do not write “the Russian neighborhood” onto a map you do not have. Pattern now. Date a geography when a controlling source exists.

Partners

Partners: synagogues and Jewish Community Centers for some of the Jewish stream; Russian Orthodox parishes some families name; evangelical and Baptist churches in some towns; no single “Russian community center” as the whole. CECLC is a department door — not the community. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Do not extract Russian-speaking staff as the interpreter or as “the community.” They may be Jewish, Ukrainian, Belarusian, or a third generation that does not want to be your culture desk. A liturgy or a JCC visit is optional professional development. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

blocks.body:
The heart of this intelligence is a refusal. Russian on the five is a door onto many peoples. Ethnic Russian peoplehood is real — language, literature, Orthodox memory for some, a state that did harm and a state some people still defend. It is not permission to file a Ukrainian, a Tajik, or a Soviet Jew under one folk costume.

In this state

Jewish peoplehood in the 1970s–90s stream is not “Russian culture with a menorah.” Ukrainian households that use Russian are not a round-up for this page. Evangelical Russians may organize life around a church in a town that has never heard the word CLAS.

In Minnesota another fact sits on the same desk: many of these households are read as white. The building’s unmarked default will skip the interpreter, skip the Cyrillic notice, and call that fairness. That skip is the gate. White appearance is not English proficiency and not the absence of a people.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.

blocks.body:
Disaggregation. The first grammar. If you cannot name the stream, you do not have a household yet.

Patronymic

Given name, father’s name as a middle element, family name. Dropping it invents a person. Filing it wrong invents a person. Ask.

Formality and titles

First name plus patronymic is respectful address in Russian. First name only can be too familiar with an elder. English “hi guys” is not a translation.

Hospitality

Tea, food, time in some rooms. Refusing everything can read as cold. You still keep medical and legal clocks.

State memory

For some, a Soviet past means you do not volunteer extra facts to a government desk. For some, the Russian Federation is still the frame. For some, 2022 ended that sentence. You do not interrogate loyalty. You do the form.

Church, synagogue, none

A parish, a shul, or a Baptist church may be the actual information channel. It is not “the community.” Do not make clergy the case plan unless this family asked.

Directness

Some Russian-speaking rooms will say the hard sentence without Minnesota Nice. That is not hostility. Follow this room. Do not punish candor and do not invent a Slavic personality.

blocks.body:
Orthodox Nativity and Pascha follow the Julian calendar for many Russian Orthodox households — often later than Western Christmas and Easter. Schedule around them when you can. They are not a day off the work. They are literacy.

Calendar

Jewish High Holidays, Passover, and other calendar days matter in the Jewish stream. They are not “Russian holidays.” Open the Jewish calendar if that is the household.

9 May — Victory Day in Soviet and Russian memory of 1945 — is real for some elders and a political fight for others after 2022. Listen. Do not put a victory parade on a case note. Do not lecture.

1991 is literacy, not a holiday. 24 February 2022 is current structure for some families. Do not put “Fall of Saigon party” energy — or a Ukraine-war slogan — on a case note.

New Year’s Eve (Novy God) was the large Soviet winter holiday and still is for some secular families. A calendar click on this program is literacy for scheduling. It is not community engagement.

There is no Compass education table for “Russian speakers.” Pattern now — date the number when a controlling source exists. Do not invent a rate.

School and language

Soviet and post-Soviet credentials were often high — engineering, medicine, teaching — and not always recognized here. A person who was a professional in 1994 and a warehouse worker in 1996 is not a personality. Children of that stream may be in English-dominant schools with a parent who still cannot run an IEP in English.

Elders may be LEP and fully literate in Cyrillic. Professionals and the U.S.-born may not need an interpreter and may still have a parent who does. Do not skip the interpreter because the adult in the lobby is white, employed, or accent-light.

A parent who speaks fluent Russian and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only form is the gate. Put Russian on the line. Confirm it is Russian, not Ukrainian.

Shoes off in some homes. Follow the household. Accept a little tea or food if offered. Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time.

In the home

Elders first. Formal address until invited. Flowers in odd numbers for some living-room visits is a pattern you do not need to perform; you do need to not mock it.

Time

Do not walk into a living room and photograph an icon corner, a Sabbath table, or a family photograph wall. Do not touch ritual objects.

On-time for appointments. Traffic and multi-household logistics are real. Courtesy-yes then no-show happens when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

Do not enter a parish, synagogue, or church as a researcher. Guest, if invited.

Russian is on the five. It is not Ukrainian. It is not Belarusian. It is not “former Soviet.” An interpreter labeled Russian who is the wrong language for this household is still a closed door — and after 2022, a political door. Confirm. CLAS: still book a qualified interpreter. A list is not the person and not the dialect.

Language

Cyrillic literacy and Latin literacy are not the same. Many elders read Russian in Cyrillic and do not read the English PDF. Some U.S.-born adults do not read Cyrillic. A “Russian notice” in Latin transliteration can still be a closed door. Put the language they read on the line.

Elders may be LEP. Professionals may not be. White appearance is not English. Do not take a light accent as “no interpreter needed” without asking.

A direct answer may be the point, not rudeness. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan.

Do not make a Russian-speaking coworker the interpreter.

Orthodox chant is liturgy, not a playlist. Jewish music — liturgical and popular — belongs to the Jewish stream, not to a “Russian mix.” Bard song, Soviet-era popular music, and contemporary pop exist. Evangelical rooms have their own hymn and chorus life.

Variation

A playlist is not engagement. A funeral or a liturgy is not staff entertainment. Knowing that music splits along stream will stop you from putting one YouTube mix on a Heritage Month table and calling it this door.

Named variation is the point. An Orthodox memorial, a Jewish wedding, and a Baptist hymn night are not one “Russian culture night” you can BCC.

blocks.body:
Hockey, soccer, figure skating, and chess carry prestige in some post-Soviet families. Ordinary school sport is ordinary for the second generation. Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see.

blocks.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

Named harms

Alcohol harm and family violence exist in some households in this language door. They are not “the culture.” They are not a Slavic joke. You follow the law. You still see a household, not a crime scene walking in. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

Elder isolation is real for some post-Soviet elders: thin English, adult children at work, winter, no single community center that holds everyone. A missed appointment can be a bus and a language, not noncompliance.

The Russian Federation’s anti-LGBTQ legal climate is current structure for some families. Queer and trans Russian-speakers exist in Minnesota. Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture.

Immigration status fear is real for some recent arrivals. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance.

Do not treat every Russian speaker as one origin or one politics. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

There is no Minnesota Compass cultural-community profile for Russian. Do not invent one to make this spine look like Hmong or Somali.

Counts

Minnesota Compass immigration table: about 6,483 foreign-born from Russia. Date the table you open. That is not a count of Russian speakers. It is not Jewish. It is not Ukrainian. It is not the third generation born here.

What the count is not

Star Tribune, 31 July 2025, on languages spoken at home: German, French, Chinese, Russian, and Arabic each represent about 2% of Minnesotans who speak a language other than English at home. The same reporting said Vietnamese, Chinese, and Russian home-speaker populations had stayed about the same. Date that article. ACS vintages disagree. Date the vintage.

Minnesota Secretary of State voter materials include Russian. That is operations evidence that the state already treats this language as a public-contact fact. It is not a population.

Compass Ukrainian: about 22,570 (ACS 2019–2023). Do not add it to 6,483 and call the sum “Russian-speaking Minnesota.” A rate is not the person. Pattern now — date the number when a controlling source exists.

blocks.body:
This is a compact learning path built from the full Salvadoran Minnesota cultural intelligence brief. Use the evidence as a starting hypothesis, not a script. The person or household in front of you is still the authority on their own life.

  • Open this brief when the origin is Salvadoran. Name El Salvador. A Mexican default is the wrong door.
  • Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity. Practitioner-based means Tuesday: origin is Salvadoran, not Mexican; Salvadoran Spanish / voseo on the interpreter line if it matters in the room; two surnames; no child as interpreter; no harvesting Salvadoran or Latino staff; do not collect status you do not need; TPS is structure not a personality; Greater Minnesota 23.3 percent is not an afterthought. Employee groups may fact-check. They do not veto civil-war memory, TPS, ICE climate, or the fact that this is not Mexican because a Minimization room is uncomfortable. Minnesota Nice deletes facts.
  • Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): 17,571; Twin Cities 76.7 percent; Greater Minnesota 23.3 percent. Age 17 or younger 48.5 percent; 65+ suppressed on Compass — do not invent it; foreign-born 43.9 percent; language other than English (5+) 79.1 percent; English less than very well 39.0 percent; high school or higher (25+) 62.1 percent; bachelor’s or higher 17.0 percent; median household income about $79,911; poverty 5.9 percent; owner 55.9 percent; average household 3.79. Date Compass. Do not invent other rates.
  • Nothing from the depth this program requires was kept at full depth. This copy is a living candidate: staff keep a stable doorway until you or an Equity Director in the administration promote.
blocks.heading: How to use this guide

blocks.body:
This brief is about Salvadoran Minnesota as a people — salvadoreño, salvadoreña — not as a Mexican variant and not as the Latino / Hispanic umbrella. Civil war (1980–1992) and Temporary Protected Status are literacy for the desk, not a speech you give the family. Spanish is not one Spanish. Voseo is ordinary in Salvadoran rooms. A Mexican interpreter can still be a closed door. This is not Mexican. It is not Guatemalan. It is not Puerto Rican. Shared Spanish is not shared culture. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

Who this is

Open the Latino umbrella only as adjacent. That page is the mash and the CLAS Spanish line. This page is Salvadoran. If you leave this door and file the household under “Latino” or under Mexican because that is the Minnesota default, you have left this door.

Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts the Salvadoran cultural community at 17,571. Twin Cities 76.7 percent; Greater Minnesota 23.3 percent — not an afterthought. About 48.5 percent age 17 or younger. Compass suppresses 65+ in this vintage — do not invent it. Foreign-born 43.9 percent. Language other than English (age 5+) 79.1 percent; English less than “very well” 39.0 percent. Date the number you use. Compass does not split an indigenous-language count on this profile. Do not invent one. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A 1980s arrival who came through the war, a TPS holder whose status is a clock, a U.S.-born nurse, a Greater Minnesota factory household, an evangelical grandmother, a college student who uses English with friends and voseo with an uncle, a person who will not open the door because a relative can be moved — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

blocks.body:
Salvadoran peoplehood is not a Mexican origin story with a different flag. El Salvador is the smallest mainland republic in Central America. Pipil / Nahua history was largely mestizo-ized by the colony and the coffee state; do not invent a Minnesota indigenous-language count Compass does not have, and do not copy K’iche’ from the Guatemalan page onto this one. Ask this household.

History for the meeting

Spanish colonial rule, independence with the other Central American republics (15 September 1821), a coffee oligarchy, and the twentieth-century state that went to war with its own people — that is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a pupusa, a volcano, or a Heritage Month sentence.

What people brought

Writing in Spanish is the ordinary public literacy. Some elders read Spanish. Some do not. Some U.S.-born adults do not read Spanish either. Oral skill is not print. Salvadoran Spanish is not Mexican Spanish.

What people brought: language (including voseo), kinship, Catholic and later evangelical church, work knowledge, remittance as obligation, a memory of a war the United States funded. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Latino” checkbox, often one interpreter labeled Spanish — usually Mexican — and a lobby that had not studied TPS.

Homeland is El Salvador — departments people name, San Salvador, the coast, the interior. Confirm the place if they name it. Do not referee Santa Ana versus San Miguel in a waiver meeting. Listen.

Homeland

The U.S. Salvadoran map is California (Los Angeles among the named hubs), the D.C.–Maryland–Virginia corridor, Texas, New York, and also Minnesota. Those hubs are not this map. Secondary migration and family pulled people here.

Minnesota

In Minnesota: Twin Cities 76.7 percent, Greater Minnesota 23.3 percent (Compass ACS 2019–2023). Greater Minnesota is not an afterthought. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume a plant town is Guatemalan by default. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to El Salvador. A Greater Minnesota household is still this people.

blocks.body:
If 1975 is the foundational event of Vietnamese Minnesota, the Salvadoran civil war (1980–1992) is the foundational political event of Salvadoran Minnesota. Archbishop Óscar Romero was assassinated on 24 March 1980. The United States backed the government. People fled. That is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. It is not an icebreaker. Do not ask a person to narrate killing for your professional development.

Foundational events

Peace Accords, 16 January 1992. Later streams carry family reunification, work, disasters, and Temporary Protected Status — including after the 2001 earthquakes — as a clock that reorganizes Tuesday. TPS is structure. It is not a personality. It is not a reason to collect status you do not need, and it is a reason a form that feels like enforcement will empty the lobby.

Who you meet

The desk in 2026 does not only meet a 1980s arrival. It meets U.S.-born children — Compass foreign-born 43.9 percent — translating for parents, mixed-status households, TPS holders, and a person who has lived here since childhood and still cannot get Salvadoran Spanish in the lobby. If you only know “immigrant,” you will miss them. If you only know “Mexican,” you will mash them.

Enforcement is current structure. When TPS is threatened, or raids are rumored, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. That is not noncompliance.

Familismo is a hypothesis, not a personality. Elders often speak first. Adult children may be in the same week as a waiver meeting, a shift, and a school conference. Compass: average household size about 3.79. Still not always a nuclear English form. Who cares for a child may not match the waiver checkbox. Ask who should be in the room.

Who is in the household

TPS and mixed-status are structure: a U.S.-citizen child, a parent on TPS, a sibling without status, an aunt who works service. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat unmatched last names, a grandmother as caregiver, or a missing SSN as fraud until you have a reason. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

Who speaks

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child with the best English. That child is not the qualified interpreter. CLAS still stands. Using a child as the go-between is a closed door and a harm. Book the interpreter. Ask who should be in the room.

Minnesota law still stands. Domestic violence is not culture. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

blocks.body:
Catholic and a large evangelical / Pentecostal stream both live in Salvadoran Minnesota. The parish or the iglesia may be the trusted channel for information, mutual aid, and a room people will enter when they will not enter yours. Romero is literacy for the desk — 24 March 1980 — not a piety ranking you assign in the lobby. Our Lady of Guadalupe is Mexican Catholic literacy. Do not install it as the default on this page. Ask.

Streams

Do not make a priest or a pastor the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one church and call it consultation. Do not treat evangelical growth as the evolved version of Catholic.

Practice

Holy Week, funerals, and fiesta obligation can collide with your calendar. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it. Do not photograph an altar.

Help that looks like a report is not help. Religious framing of disability, mental health, or gender can sit next to a fierce wish for services. You can hold both.

blocks.body:
Elders first. A handshake is common in many rooms. A slight nod with an older person is safer than a hard first-name hello you assume is warmth. Follow this room.

Titles

Titles until invited: Señor, Señora, Don, Doña. Use the last name you were given — and remember there may be two. Do not use a first name with an elder because the form printed it. Usted is respect with strangers and elders; voseo is ordinary among familiars. A qualified interpreter matches register. You do not correct it.

This room

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default. A hug from staff is not warmth if the household did not offer it.

blocks.body:
Two surnames is the default in much of Salvadoran Spanish-language naming: apellido paterno then apellido materno. A U.S. database that keeps one surname invents a person. That invented name then follows them through MHCP, child welfare, and school. It is a gate.

How to file

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Do not drop accents as a joke. Given names may be Spanish, English, or both. Some people use a middle given name as the call-name. Ask.

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default. Do not invent a hyphen and then punish the person when the hyphen moves.

blocks.body:
Minnesota holds a Salvadoran community large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment. Compass: 17,571 (ACS 2019–2023). Twin Cities 76.7 percent; Greater Minnesota 23.3 percent — not an afterthought. Do not write this people as a Minneapolis anecdote and do not write them as a Mexican leftover.

Places

Places, not a blob: Twin Cities corridors and first-ring suburbs; Greater Minnesota towns with work and housing. Pupusa shops and markets are public life. They are not consultation. A food visit does not make you the expert.

Partners

Partners: parishes and evangelical churches families name; rural parish and worker centers — name the local one; do not assume Minneapolis. CLUES is a Twin Cities door, not the whole community. CECLC is a department door, not the people. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Salvadoran staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. A fiesta or a Romero commemoration is optional professional development if you are invited. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

blocks.body:
To be Salvadoran in Minnesota is to be a people with a small country and a long memory of a war the United States funded, then building a life in a cold state that filed you under Latino and often under Mexican. Face, kin, remittance, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

In this state

Spanish is not one Spanish. Voseo is ordinary. A Mexican interpreter who does not hear this household is a closed door.

The Mexican default in this state is a count fact on another page. It is a harm on this one when staff copy Guadalupe, norteño, and Mexican Spanish onto a Salvadoran household.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.

Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Salvadoran Minnesotans 25 and older, about 62.1 percent high school or higher; about 17.0 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. About 43.9 percent of the community is foreign-born. Among those 5 and older, 79.1 percent speak a language other than English; 39.0 percent speak English less than “very well.” That is a language gate, not a culture clash. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Salvadoran Spanish and limited English is not illiterate. Some elders read Spanish. Some do not. The English-only form is the gate. A Mexican-Spanish notice is not automatically this household’s Spanish. Do not use a child as interpreter.

Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room that treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of language access plus enforcement fear plus a school that never learned the second surname. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter.

blocks.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

Named harms

ICE, TPS, and enforcement climate are structure. Mixed-status households skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved or when TPS is a clock. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need. SSN on the first screen is a gate.

The Mexican default in this state will talk over this household if you let the umbrella page do this page’s job. Spanish is not one Spanish.

Gang discourse in U.S. media — including MS-13 as a story that began among Salvadoran refugee youth in Los Angeles — is HISTORY and a named harm in enforcement. A last name is not a gang file. Do not score a Minnesota child on a cousin’s decade or a cable-news segment. Follow law. Still see a family.

Machismo is a named harm, not a joke and not “that’s culture.” Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. LGBTQ Salvadoran Minnesotans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

blocks.body:
This is a compact learning path built from the full Thai Minnesota cultural intelligence brief. Use the evidence as a starting hypothesis, not a script. The person or household in front of you is still the authority on their own life.

  • Open this brief when the household is Thai. Book Thai. A restaurant visit is not consultation.
  • Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity. Practitioner-based means Tuesday: book Thai, not Lao, not Hmong; do not file this household under Thai border camps; Greater Minnesota is not an afterthought; no harvesting Thai staff. Employee groups may fact-check. They do not veto 30.6 percent LEP, 17.8 percent poverty, or the camp mash because a Minimization room is uncomfortable.
  • Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Thai ancestry near 6,738. About 60.8 percent Twin Cities, 39.2 percent Greater Minnesota. About 37.5 percent age 17 or younger; 65+ about 4.9 percent. Foreign-born about 37.4 percent. Language other than English (5+) about 66.7 percent; English less than “very well” about 30.6 percent. High school or higher (25+) about 86.4 percent; bachelor’s or higher about 29.5 percent. Median household income about $72,888 in 2022 dollars. Poverty 17.8 percent. Owner-occupied about 46.4 percent. Average household size about 3.15. Date Compass. Do not invent other rates. 30.6 percent LEP is a language gate. 17.8 percent poverty is not a model-minority skip.
  • Nothing from the depth this program requires was kept at full depth. This copy is a living candidate: staff keep a stable doorway until you or an Equity Director in the administration promote.
blocks.heading: How to use this guide

blocks.body:
This brief is about Thai people as a people of Thailand — the lowland state history, Theravada wats, a language related to Lao and not interchangeable with it — and as a Minnesota community Compass counts near 6,738 (ACS 2019–2023). This is not Hmong. This is not Lao. Camps in Thailand — Ban Vinai, Mae La, and others — held Hmong and Karen families after wars this people did not fight as those files. Do not file a Thai household under that war. If the household is Hmong, open Hmong Minnesota. If Lao, open Lao Minnesota. If Thai, book Thai.

Who this is

This is not a Census “Asian” mash. It is not Khmer. It is not Vietnamese. Shared continent is not shared culture. Songkran is not Hmong New Year and not Tết. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 6,738; Twin Cities 60.8 percent; Greater Minnesota 39.2 percent; age 17 or younger 37.5 percent; 65+ about 4.9 percent; foreign-born 37.4 percent; among those 5 and older, English only about 33.3 percent, language other than English about 66.7 percent, English less than “very well” about 30.6 percent; high school or higher (25+) about 86.4 percent; bachelor’s or higher about 29.5 percent; median household income about $72,888 in 2022 dollars; poverty 17.8 percent; owner-occupied 46.4 percent; average household size about 3.15; individuals living alone about 18.6 percent. Female about 59.7 percent. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A wat household in the Twin Cities, a Greater Minnesota restaurant family, an Isan speaker, a Bangkok-origin professional, a U.S.-born child translating for a parent, a marriage-stream household far from a Thai-speaking neighbor — share a Compass row and do not share a Tuesday.

How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

blocks.body:
Thai peoplehood is older than the name Thailand (1939), older than 1932, and older than the restaurant file. Siam; kingdoms; a modern nation that marks itself as never colonized by a European power — that national narrative is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. It is not a virtue ranking against neighbors who were colonized.

History for the meeting

Thai language is related to Lao. Related is not interchangeable. A Lao interpreter is not the default. Isan (northeastern Thai) is a neighboring variety some families will name. Ask. Do not guess. Do not mash Hmong into this origin because camps sat on Thai soil.

What people brought

What people brought: language, Theravada practice or not, family obligation, foodways, a memory of a state that was not a camp. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, a restaurant cliché, and often a worker who has already filed them under Hmong because the building only studied the war.

Writing is Thai script. Related to Lao — not interchangeable. Many elders read Thai. Some do not. Second generation may not read it at all. A notice in Lao, or in English only, can still be a closed door. Ask.

blocks.body:
Thailand is Bangkok, the north, the south, Isan, and the places families name. Isan is related to Lao language and music — not identical, not a Lao file, not a Hmong file. Do not draw one tuk-tuk on a case note. The Malay-Muslim south is a named geography some families will name. You do not referee.

Homeland

A global diaspora: United States, Europe, the Gulf, East Asia. Minnesota is one map, not the map. Compass: about 60.8 percent Twin Cities, 39.2 percent Greater Minnesota. That Greater Minnesota share is large next to several neighboring spines. Towns with restaurants, campuses, and mixed households are on this page.

Minnesota

Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume they have been to Bangkok. Do not file this household onto a Thai border-camp map. Ban Vinai and Mae La are Hmong and Karen geographies. Open those CIs for those households.

blocks.body:
Thai Minnesota is not a 1975 airlift community. Student, marriage, restaurant and small-business, professional, and family-reunification streams built what you will meet. Cold War U.S. presence in Thailand and later ordinary immigration are literacy. They are not a Hmong Secret War sentence and not a Karen camp sentence.

Foundational events

Camps on Thai soil held other peoples. Ban Vinai, Mae La, and others are named on the Hmong and Karen spines. Filing a Thai family under that war is a closed door. Do not ask a Thai parent to narrate a camp they did not live. Do not skip this page because the building only trained on 1975.

Who you meet

U.S.-born children sit in a young age structure — Compass 37.5 percent age 17 or younger. The desk meets a child with English and a parent who still cannot get Thai in the lobby. 30.6 percent LEP is the gate.

If you only know “restaurant,” you will miss the wat household, the Greater Minnesota marriage-stream family, and the professional who still needs this page.

blocks.body:
Elders often speak first. Filial obligation is a hypothesis, not a personality. Compass: average household size about 3.15. Multi-generation households exist. So do people who live alone (about 18.6 percent). Ask who should be in the room.

Who is in the household

Female about 59.7 percent in this Compass row is a labor and marriage-stream fact. It is not a mail-order personality, not a joke, and not a reason to skip the man in the lobby. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

Who speaks

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child with the best English. That child is not the qualified interpreter. Using a child as the go-between is a closed door and a harm. Book Thai.

Minnesota law still stands. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. Who holds the child’s medical decision may not match the English form. Ask.

blocks.body:
Theravada Buddhism is the large public stream. The wat is a center of ritual, mutual aid, and information. It is not “the community.” Some Christianity, and none, also live here. Ask. Do not assume a wat. Do not assume no wat.

Streams

Do not mash Hmong household religion or txiv neeb onto this page. Do not make a monk the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one wat and call it consultation.

Practice

Shoes off. Head high. Feet not toward a Buddha image. Do not photograph an altar. Funerals and holy days gather family. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it.

Spirit practice exists in some rooms beside Theravada. Do not treat that as folklore. Do not treat it as a case plan.
